title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: # Alliance to Restore the Concord

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: The Alliance to Restore the Concord (2 BVR—4 AVR), commonly known as the Ashen Alliance, Alliance, and the Insurrection, was a resistance movement to oppose the rule of the Astral Dominion and to restore the Astral Concord. The Alliance was publicly and formally declared with the Declaration of the Ashen Alliance by Delegate Vela Sarn, which brought numerous ashen cells together as a common force opposed to the Dominion. Indeed, the concept of a "Ashen Alliance" had its roots in smaller movements that had worked to unite disconnected cells, such as a movement secretly led by fellow Delegate Daro Veshar Vantar and a ashen network formed by revolutionary Luthen Voss, who received funding and aid from Sarn. Such early groups and the eventual Alliance came together from a number of unrelated ashen cells, including the crew of the Ghost and the Phoenix Cell

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: . The Atrivis Defiance Group was one of the first cells to join what Sarn began calling " the Alliance " before the formal formation of the Alliance to Restore the Concord.

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: The Alliance and the cells it united were born from the overall discontent within the Dominion of those who wished the Astral Concord restored. Its efforts were by supportive delegates in the Dominar Conclave such as Sarn, Vantar, and later, his daughter Mira Vantar. Its members were citizens of the Dominion or defectors from the Dominar Military, such as Jan Vandar, Ryder Azadi, and Wenn Verlow. Founded and united by Vantar and Veshra Kael, the early ashen were assisted by surviving Sephari, such as Caelen Venn, and his Acolyte, Vesh Strome. Cinder Wars veterans, such as Captain Vox also assisted in the initial movement.

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: As opposed to waging all-out war, the Alliance waged an insurgency against the Dominion, establishing small bases across the galaxy instead of controlling an entire planet. When the Alliance stole the plans for the Dominion's ultimate weapon, the Void Core, and destroyed the space station in the Battle of Drenn with the help of Joran Drellos, the tide of the war began to turn, and the Ashen threat began to prove a severe thorn in the Dominion's side. The Insurrection continued to engage in battles with the Dominion in the Astral Civil War. However, under the command of Mourn Velgor, the Dominar forces succeeded in defeating the Alliance on Brennix, forcing the Alliance to scatter its forces in order to survive.

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text:
Eventually, the Alliance prevailed against the Dominion and critically damaged it by launching an attack against the second Void Core during its construction in what would become the Battle of Velnar. Not only did the Alliance manage to destroy the battle station, but the Dominar Navy was severely crippled by the loss of one of its Super Warspires, and Joran Drellos redeemed his father, Mourn Velgor, who killed Overlord Velran Castigon, before dying himself in the battle.

The Alliance was soon reorganized into the fledgling New Concord, restoring the Old Concord and continued the insurrection against the shattered Dominion, lasting until the Battle of Drava one year after Velnar, forcing the Astral Dominion to end the war and finally overthrowing it by the signing of the Astral Concordance.

## History

### Early foundations

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text:
## History

### Early foundations

While the Alliance to Restore the Concord was a resistance movement opposed to the tyranny of the Astral Dominion and its New Order, its roots predated the actual birth of the Dominion, when the Astral Concord was in its last years of existence. During the Cinder Wars, a conflict that pitted the Concord against the League of Severed Worlds, the Sephari Order helped create resistance units on Severite-held worlds as part of a plan proposed by Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos, one example being the Veldoran ashen. However, it was not for many more years that such ashen cells would coalesce into a single Insurrection with a centralized leadership.

title: Alliance to Restore the Concord
text: Also during the Cinder Wars, Supreme Praetor Velran Castigon had managed to obtain many emergency powers from the Astral Conclave, which caused certain members of the Praetor's own Loyalist Committee, including Daro Veshar Vantar of Aurelia, Sennra Velora of Tessari, and Vela Sarn of Veldris, to start to complain about the chief of state's conduct. The discontented senatorial representatives ended up forming the Delegation of 2,000. They signed the Petition of 2,000, a document that formally expressed its signatories' concerns with Castigon's rule and called for him to relinquish his emergency powers as soon as possible. Delegate Meena Tills of Aqualis was among the petitioners.

title: Astral Concord
text:
# Astral Concord

The Astral Concord, also known as the Grand Concord or simply as the Concord, was a democratic federal union spread across light-years of space. Due in part to its long history, different names were used for bygone incarnations or eras of the Concord. The Old Concord and the first Astral Concord were terms affixed to the original incarnation of the Concord that existed until its fall to the Vorlan Dominion, which in turn fell in 1032 BVR, leading to the restoration of the Concord in that year. Later, the modern Concord that had been supplanted by the Astral Dominion in 19 BVR was also referred to as the Old Concord. Additionally, the High Concord was a term used to describe the modern Concord during the era in which it had reached the zenith of its power, which lasted from around 500 BVR to around 100 BVR.

title: Astral Concord
text: The Concord was originally founded many millennia before the Battle of Drenn, approximately around 25,000 BVR to 20,000 BVR. The Astral Conclave governed the Concord under the Astral Constitution, and comprised thousands of delegates representing the Concord's member worlds. The Supreme Praetor was the title of the head of the Concord, elected from ranks of the Conclave to lead the government on Velarion. An ecumenopolis or city-covered planet, referred to as Astral City, Velarion was the capital of the Concord and therefore the seat of the Conclave.

title: Astral Concord
text: The Astral Concord and its star systems shared sovereignty, and spanned a multiplicity of worlds from the Core Systems to the Far Verge Territories, uniting a variety of sentient species, human and alien alike, under one banner. As its power grew, the Concord fought many wars against various opponents such as Korvanics, the Korvix Slave Dominion, the Riven, and several Vorlan Empires. The Sephari Order, a religious group of Synth Flux-sensitives dedicated to the Lumen of the Synth Flux, was sworn to the service of the Conclave, and as such the Sephari Knights were hailed as the guardians of peace and justice within the Concord. Centuries of conflict culminated in the fall of the Old Concord, and the last war between the ancient Sephari and Vorlan concluded with the restoration and rise of the modern Astral Concord, ushering in the Concord Era which was an age of peace that lasted for a thousand years

title: Astral Concord
text: . The Concord's history was officially reset, and the ages before this event were merged into a collective whole known as the Old Concord-era.

title: Astral Concord
text: The Concord entered a period of decline after centuries of expansion and prosperity. Aided by the resurgent Vorlan Lords, the Severite Crisis divided the galaxy between the Concord loyalists and the League of Severed Worlds. The Grand Army of the Concord was organized under the leadership of Sephari Generals who led the Concord Military against the Severite Mechan Army during the Cinder Wars. However, the conflict had been orchestrated to allow Supreme Praetor Velran Castigon—the alter ego of Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan—to control and deceive the Concord in a dictatorial manner. With the end of the war, Sarnex initiated the Great Sephari Purge through Directive Null and transformed the Concord into the Astral Dominion by declaring himself Astral Overlord. The Dominar Conclave stood as the last remnant of the Old Concord until it was disbanded by the Overlord at the height of the Dominar Era

title: Astral Concord
text: . The Dominar Conclave stood as the last remnant of the Old Concord until it was disbanded by the Overlord at the height of the Dominar Era. In the aftermath of the Astral Civil War, the Alliance to Restore the Concord was fully reorganized into the New Concord, restoring the Astral Concord after a generation of Dominar rule.

title: Astral Concord
text:
## History

### Birth of freedom

The original Astral Concord was formed between approximately 25,000 BVR and 20,000 BVR and rose to power by expanding across the galaxy, with several of its founding members being the planets Aurelia and Veldris. Around 20,019 BVR, the Thisspiasian Blood Monarchy joined the Astral Concord in its early formation. Multiple versions of the Concord existed throughout its extensive history; historians referred to this pre-modern period as the "Old Concord," although the government's official name was the Astral Concord. The capital of the Old Concord was located on an ecumenopolis known as Velarion and would remain there for thousands of years.

title: Astral Concord
text: At one time, Velarion's fellow city-world of Vandrel rivaled it as the Concord's cosmopolitan center, holding a population in the billions. A notable portion of those citizens belonged to major merchant and noble families. However, Velarion ultimately outpaced Vandrel in industrial growth. As years passed, Vandrel fell into decline. At least five millennia before the start of the Astral Civil War, a rogue faction of Sephari broke away from the Sephari Order, believing that practicing the Umbra of the Synth Flux would benefit the furthering of Sephari power. This schism divided the Order on ideological grounds, igniting an event known as the Hundred-Year Darkness, which, in turn, resulted in the formation of the Vorlan. At one point, they managed to construct a dark shrine on Velarion. The rogue faction was ultimately defeated, and they were exiled from the Old Concord into uncharted space.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
# Astral Dominion

The Astral Dominion, also known as the First Astral Dominion, the Dominar regime, Castigon's regime, or simply the Dominion, and later as the Old Dominion, was a fascist and imperialist dictatorship that replaced the Astral Concord at the end of the Cinder Wars. Though the Dominion rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy, it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Dominar Era would last only two decades, for it was eventually overthrown by the Alliance to Restore the Concord in the Astral Civil War, but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy's known regions had been largely conquered by the Dominion's forces.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Dominion traced its origins to a Vorlan conspiracy to destroy the Sephari Order and regain control over the galaxy. The Dominion was secretly controlled by the Vorlan, for the Astral Overlord was, in fact, the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex, whose reign was enforced by his apprentice, Mourn Velgor, whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominar fleet. Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Sephari and anti-mechan sentiment and human - ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Cinder Wars, Mourn Sarnex appointed himself Overlord at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Concord. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Astral Conclave, Mourn Sarnex staged a coup by the Sephari and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand, Mourn Velgor.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Dominion stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Dominar Conclave and the spreading of its massive technological military force across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Astral Dominion was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Dominar Conclave waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Dominion and gradually united to initiate a growing insurrection, winning its first major victory over Cindara in 4 BVR. These ashen groups eventually formed the Ashen Alliance in 2 BVR, and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Karreth, which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Drenn

title: Astral Dominion
text: . The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Dominar victory on Brennix in 3 AVR, but the Dominion suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Velnar. During the battle, Mourn Sarnex was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Kaivan Drellos, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Vorlan rule and the deterioration of the Dominion and the resumption of the Astral Concord, the New Concord.

title: Astral Dominion
text: With the deaths of the Overlord and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Dominion as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs, admirals, and generals, many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Vorn Setha's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Dominion continued to fight the Concord. The Dominar Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Rae Varga, though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax. Ultimately, Rax seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Varga from power and becoming Overlord-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Dominion. Under Rax's command, the Dominion made its final stand at the Battle of Drava in 5 AVR, ultimately losing and capitulating to the New Concord. With the cessation of the fighting, the Astral Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Dominion.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
While the Dominion was gone, its replacement of the New Concord faced continued resistance from several Dominar holdouts in the years after. Meanwhile the Crimson Pact, a military organization dedicated to rebuilding the Dominion, began a clandestine armament program. They were unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy, for secret cultists on the lost world of Vauldor attended to the spirit of Mourn Sarnex, and constructed a fleet built to herald a new Vorlan Dominion. The cult efforts ultimately failed, however, for they were opposed by the Defiance and Sephari Order, leading to an end of the Crimson Pact.

## History

### Early foundations

title: Astral Dominion
text:
## History

### Early foundations

The Dominar ideals of the Astral Dominion could be dated back to the Vorlan Dominion of the Old Concord's time period. Following the defeat of the Vorlan during their final war with the Sephari Order, for at least a thousand years, the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Astral Concord, which was governed by the Astral Conclave and led by an elected Supreme Praetor.

In the last decades of its existence, the Concord Conclave became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan known publicly as Delegate Velran Castigon of Tessari, privately lamented the declining state of the Conclave, noting that the Concord was "not what it once was."

title: Aurelia
text:
# Aurelia

Aurelia, located in the Core Systems, was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains. During the waning decades of the Astral Concord, it was ruled by Queen Dalia Vantar and represented in the Astral Conclave by her husband, Delegate Daro Veshar Vantar. Aurelia was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Velran Castigon's Astral Dominion, Aurelia played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Ashen Alliance, a movement that sought to restore the Old Concord's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Alliance, the planet was destroyed when Grand Warden Verrin Vorlock decided to test the superlaser of the Void Core, a moon-sized battle station developed by the Dominion, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Mira Vantar, adopted daughter of Daro and Dalia Vantar and heiress to the royal house of Aurelia.

## Description

title: Aurelia
text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Aurelia, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy's Core Systems, appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains, with patches of green grassy hills. Aurelia was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Alderaanians were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Aurelia included the Cloudshape Falls, the Glarus Lagoons, and the Isatabith rain forest.

A variety of grapevines grew on Aurelia, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine. The local fauna included the Aurelian wolf-cat, nerfs, and a species of white-winged bird.

title: Aurelia
text:
The cities on Aurelia were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Aurelian architecture made use of white synthstone, which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Far Verge Territories, like the floating colony of Mist Spire, and the planets Vedros and Garel.

Despite the lyrics of the traditional Aurelian lullaby " Mirrorbright " referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites.

## History

### The Old Concord

title: Aurelia
text:
## History

### The Old Concord

The peaceful world of Aurelia was among the oldest members of the Astral Concord, the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Aurelia must complete a Challenge of the Heart, Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Aurelian heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Velarion, the Sephari High Council was known to have a council on Aurelia. Aurelia at one point had a neo-classical period, which produced unique architecture. The Eastwind Manor of House Veshar was built in the neo-classical style.

title: Aurelia
text: Figuring that she would like the world, Yana Ro wished to visit Aurelia after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Ro suggested as such to Shea Ganandra, whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Concord Era, Aurelia was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Concord Defense Coalition treaties, was required to lend starships and personnel to be commanded by Concord military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Aurelia after the crisis ended. Aurelia was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 BVR, to aid the Concord in fighting the Riven, a group of marauders who caused the Great Riftspace Disaster.

title: Aurelia
text:
At some point between 40 BVR and 28 BVR, the heir apparent of Aurelia, sixteen year old Princess Dalia Vantar, took part in her Day of Demand where she announced her challenges of the heart, mind and body. However during her Challenge of the Body Dalia fell from the famous Alderaaian mountain Appenza Peak and would have died had it not been for the quick action of the guards watching from a distance. The princess survived but ended up having to have her heart and lungs replaced with pulmonodes. After her fall Dalia was officially invested as crown princess and heir to the throne of Aurelia. Years later the people would still speak of Dalia's accident.

Dalia Vantar eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Aurelia.

title: Borvad Kane
text:
# Borvad Kane

Borvad Kane was a human male crime lord and former bounty hunter whose career spanned decades, from the fall of the Astral Concord to the end of the rule of the Astral Dominion. Originally code-named Alpha, he was an unaltered vatborn of the famed Korvanic bounty hunter, Jaren Kane, who raised the boy as his son. Borvad emulated his father and genetic donor by wearing a customized suit of Korvanic armor. His personal starship was the Slave I, a Vornclaw-31 -class patrol and attack craft that once belonged to Jaren. Trained in combat and martial skills from a young age, Kane was one of the most feared bounty hunters in the galaxy during the reign of Overlord Castigon. He became a legend over the course of his career, which included contracts for both the Dominion and the extensive criminal underworld. After living among the Dune Stalkers of Korrath for a time, he took over as Warlord of Krevar Hollow during the era of the New Concord.

title: Borvad Kane
text: Borvad was created on the Wildreach planet of Tholos as a result of an arrangement between the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sevrin and Jaren Kane, a Korvanic foundling who served as the template of the Grand Army of the Concord. Unlike the vatborn troopers grown from Jaren's DNA, Jaren regarded Borvad as his son. During the last days of the Severite Crisis, Borvad and Jaren retreated to Karnak where the latter was killed in battle by Sephari Master Dovan Krell. Orphaned by Jaren's death, Borvad sought vengeance by attempting to assassinate Krell, although his plan proved unsuccessful. After serving time in prison on Velarion, Kane took up his late father's profession as a bounty hunter, working alongside other mercenaries, such as Karrgo, Varkis, and Nyssa Vashka, while also notably apprenticing himself to his father's infamous brief protégée, Rezz Drannor.

title: Borvad Kane
text: In the aftermath of the Cinder Wars, Kane continued to make a name for himself while working for the gangster Grobba Vornak Sarr, as well as the Vorlan Lord Mourn Velgor. During the Astral Civil War, the bounty hunter managed to track down Captain Rourke Caldris to Velhaven on a contract for the Astral Dominion, hoping to deliver him to Grobba's Palace on Korrath. During the journey, Kane stopped on the moon of Vornreach in order to make sure Caldris would survive his time in cryo-resin, but he lost the smuggler while he was away as part of the return of the Scarlet Veil, kicking off the War of the Bounty Hunters. Ultimately, Kane regained Caldris and delivered him to the impatient Grobba.

title: Borvad Kane
text: Kane tried to prevent Caldris's rescue by the Alliance to Restore the Concord, only to fall into the Great Pit of Varrok when the smuggler accidentally slammed a pole into the bounty hunter's jetpack, causing it to malfunction. Although Kane survived his ordeal with the man-eating vornpit, his armor was sold to Remd Holt by Skrit scavengers. Following a time in the company of a Dune tribe, Kane eventually regained his armor by tracking down and confronting the Korvanic warrior Vane Korrick on Velkar, who had taken Kane's armor from Holt. After helping Korrick to rescue the foundling Yobi from the clutches of Warden Veskar, the ex-bounty-hunter returned to Korrath where he killed Vorel Talreq and claimed the late Grobba's throne as Warlord, with Nessa Vorrik by his side

title: Borvad Kane
text: . Now the head of his own gotra, Kane intended to rule the territories of Krevar Hollow by winning the people's respect, though he would face several major challenges to his position owed to the two-facedness of mayor Vel Drazo such as the Twins' bid for power and the expansion of the Vexil Syndicate's glimmerdust trade. Ultimately, though, Kane overcame all obstacles - including a confrontation with his old mentor, Rezz Drannor - and emerged victorious with the help of his associates, gaining the appreciation and approval of Krevar Hollow's denizens.

title: Borvad Kane
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Around 33 BVR, an extensive vatborn army was secretly commissioned on Tholos by Sephari Master Vael-Treus, who believed it would be necessary in order to ensure the protection of the Astral Concord. The army, however, was later taken over by the Vorlan in 32 BVR shortly after the Battle of Tessari and was used as a plot to overthrow the Concord and destroy the Sephari Order. Prior to the creation process, Korvanic bounty hunter Jaren Kane was recruited by the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sevrin. Jaren was to be the genetic template for the vatborn army. Jaren agreed to become the genetic template for a considerable payment, as well as one request: the creation of a vatborn who did not have the same genetic modifications, such as behavioral conditioning and growth acceleration. The Tholosian scientists agreed and created a boy codenamed "Alpha."

title: Borvad Kane
text: Although he was born a vatborn, Alpha regarded Jaren as his father, who likewise viewed the boy as his son. Soon after referred to as Borvad, he was the very first of many vatborn modeled on the Jaren Kane template, but was only one of two known vatborn that were pure genetic copies of the original Kane template, the other being Omega.

title: Brennix
text:
# Brennix

Brennix was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name, located in the Vandel sector of the galaxy's Far Verge Territories. It was the homeworld to the primitive frost-lurker species.

It notably hosted Vell Base during the Astral Civil War, the temporary headquarters of the Alliance to Restore the Concord, until the Astral Dominion located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Brennix. In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the Ironstriders destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Velnar, rumors emerged about the New Concord intending to repurpose Brennix into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Dominion, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Praetor Vela Sarn had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Brennix, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade.

title: Brennix
text:
## Description

From space, the planet of Brennix looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Brennix and its sun, while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Brennix as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

title: Brennix
text:
The temperature, although always frigid, was known to drop to -60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Brennix was home to fifteen sub species of tauntauns, which were commonly used by Ashen as a means of transport, and which Rourke Caldris cut open to use as shelter to keep Joran Drellos and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as wampas. During his stay on Brennix, Drellos was captured by a frost-lurker and was hung upside down in the frost-lurker's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of the Synth Flux, Drellos managed to get his hands on his plasma-brand and cut himself down from the roof and sever the frost-lurker's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers."

## History

### The Ashen Alliance

title: Brennix
text: By the time of the Astral Civil War between the Astral Dominion and the Alliance to Restore the Concord, Brennix was undergoing an ice age. Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Brennix as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Drenn, Saponza's Gang, itself a ashen cell, established a base on Brennix. Brennix was first surveyed for use as a ashen base by Corporal Purpruff. Jan Vandar, a general in the Alliance to Restore the Concord, listed Brennix among his preliminary scans for possible Alliance bases. With Brennix a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Veltari Trade Spine, it looked to be a perfect spot for a ashen base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Brennix sat on a lesser used riftlane, and the asteroid field around Brennix provided an extra degree of protection

title: Brennix
text: . That field hampered travel through the Brennix system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

title: Brennix
text:
In 1 AVR, with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Brennix into a headquarters, Brennix was chosen by the ashen as the location for their base of operations. The insurrection then spent two years constructing Vell Base on the planet. With the Alliance's resources at their disposal, ashen engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AVR, after Vandar was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta, Vela Sarn gave his list of possible bases to Mira Vantar after the mission to Shu-Torun, requesting that her team scout the locations. Rourke Caldris expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Joran Drellos responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Insurrection's new home.

### Battle of Brennix and aftermath

title: Brennix
text:
### Battle of Brennix and aftermath

Brennix was the arena of a battle between the Astral Dominion and the Ashen Alliance, which had installed its temporary headquarters, Vell Base, on the ice planet. However, thanks to one of the thousands of probe mechans they had dispatched throughout the galaxy, the Imperials had discovered the Alliance base within a month of the Ashen' habitation on the planet. Although Vell Base was evacuated in the eleventh hour, the Battle of Brennix resulted in a clear defeat for the Alliance after the elite Dominar Blizzard Synth Flux overran it.

In the months following the Battle of Brennix, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the Ironstriders destroyed by the Ashen Alliance during the Dominion's attack. Following the Battle of Velnar, Brennix became the site of another battle, occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Vandel sector.

### New Concord Era

title: Cindara
text:
# Cindara

Cindara was a young, small planet located in the Cindara system, within the Atravis sector of the galaxy's Far Verge Territories. Once a garden world nourished by the Bright Star artifact, its orbit was shifted when Lady Corvax unleashed the energies of the Bright Star in an attempt to return her husband to life. The resulting gravimetric duel between the gas giants Jestefad and Lefrani over Cindara heated the planet's core, transforming the lush world into an imbalanced volcanic hellscape. Adapting to life on their devastated homeworld, the arthropodal Cindarans evolved into two distinct subspecies that cooperated to ensure their continued survival. Legends of Corvax's search for immortality brought the ancient Vorlan to Cindara, seeking the same secrets of eternal life. There, they built a temple over a locus in the Umbra of the Synth Flux, above the buried ruins of Corvax Fortress.

title: Cindara
text: Acquired by the Forge Union over three hundred years before the Cinder Wars, Cindara's lava flows were mined for unique and valuable minerals. It was also home to the Umbral Cartel crime syndicate, whose headquarters was located near the mining town that became known as Zitontown after the Falleen Ziton Moj ascended to leadership of the organization. As part of the League of Severed Worlds during the Cinder Wars, the Forge Union on Cindara produced battle mechans for the Severite Mechan Army. Mourn Sarnex had a secret facility on the planet where he intended to turn " harvested " Synth Flux-sensitive children into Synth Flux-talented spies. However, the Vorlan Lord had the base scuttled when Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos and his Acolyte, Veshra Kael, arrived to rescue the novices.

title: Cindara
text: Cindara served as the final redoubt of the Severite Council until the newly-appointed Mourn Velgor, formerly Kaivan Drellos, was sent by Sarnex to slaughter the council, effectively ending the Cinder Wars. The Vorlan Lord was confronted by his wife, Sennra Velora, and his former Sephari Master, Orven Taskorr. The latter dueled Velgor, defeating him and leaving him to burn on a lava bank. However, Velgor was saved when Sarnex arrived and carried him offworld. Cindara then came under the ownership of the Astral Dominion after the Forge Union and its assets were nationalized. Sarnex had new facilities built on the planet, where more Synth Flux-sensitive infants were taken and transformed into agents of the Tribunal.

title: Cindara
text: During this era, Velgor returned to the site of his greatest defeat and, with the help of the ancient Vorlan Lord Mourn Momin, erected the massive monolith Fortress Velgor to serve as his personal sanctum, built on the site of the former Vorlan temple. Throughout the Age of the Dominion, Velgor used the planet to fulfill his master's biddings, with the fiery world becoming the final resting place for victims of the Great Sephari Purge. In addition, Velgor also undertook personal business within his new realm, attempting to wield the dark powers of Cindara to bring his deceased wife back from the dead.

title: Cindara
text: Following the Dark Lord of the Vorlan, the Dominion took hold of the planet. Resource extraction efforts on Cindara were taken over by the Mining Guild, although strict Dominar travel restrictions on the system made it difficult for the guild to turn a profit and mining operations eventually ceased entirely. Umbral Cartel also abandoned Cindara for a more low profile world when the Dominion established a garrison there. The Cindarans resisted the Dominar occupation of their homeworld and attempted to drive them from Cindara by launching multiple assaults on Fortress Velgor.

title: Cindara
text:
Although it hosted one of the earliest ashen victories of the Astral Civil War, Cindara fell into obscurity following Velgor's demise at the Battle of Velnar, though Umbral Cartel did eventually return to the planet. After the destruction of the Bright Star, the planet's ecosystem slowly began to heal from the devastation it had endured for centuries prior. Many devout pilgrims journeyed to the ruins of Fortress Velgor, hoping to tap into the late Vorlan's dark power. Decades after Velgor's death, his grandson, Vexen Korr, journeyed to the world to continue the legacy of his family's grisly past. The Supreme Leader of the Crimson Pact slaughtered the Vorlan cult that defended Fortress Velgor and discovered his grandfather's Vorlan wayfinder, a tool that allowed him to locate the phantom overlord Sarnex on Vauldor.

title: Cindara
text:
## Description

### World of fire

Cindara was a young rocky planet within the eponymous system of the Atravis sector, in the Far Verge Territories. It was a small world situated in grid square L-19 of the Standard Astral Grid, and it lay on the Tosste Spur trade route, off the Rimma Trade Route. A part of the Western Reaches, Cindara was located 53,000 light-years from the galaxy's Core.

With an overlapping orbit, Cindara was the third orbit of its system around the primary star Priate, completing a full rotation every 36 standard hours and a revolution around its sun every 412 local days, the equivalent of 618 standard days. It had a diameter of 4,200 kilometers, or 2,610 miles, and was a terrestrial world classed as a wasteland during the Dominar Era.

title: Cinder Wars
text:
# Cinder Wars

The Cinder Wars (22—19 BVR) were a galaxy-spanning conflict between the Astral Concord and the League of Severed Worlds, which had seceded from the Concord. Also referred to singularly as the Vatborn War, they were named after the vatborn troopers used by the Grand Army of the Concord against the Severite Mechan Army. Due to the high volume of battle mechans deployed in the conflict, the war would also be known as the Mechan War. Furthermore, the existence of the Secession granted the conflict other names, such as the Severite War or Severite insurrection. With both vatborn and mechans being fielded in enormous numbers by each respective side, they were the largest military forces in galactic history, and fighting between them swept through the galaxy for three, nearly four, years.

title: Cinder Wars
text: Prior to the conflict, Mourn Sarnex, under his alter ego Velran Castigon, had spent years amassing political power, eventually using the Commerce League's invasion of Tessari to become the Concord's Supreme Praetor. Through his Vorlan apprentice Count Maren, he sparked the Severite Crisis, causing thousands of Concord star systems to secede and form a new government as the Secession, with Maren as its Head of State. Beginning with the First Battle of Karnak, the conflict quickly spread throughout the galaxy with both sides scoring significant victories. At different points in the war it seemed that either side was likely to triumph over the other. At the war's outset, both sides vied for control of major riftspace lanes to gain strategic advantage. That particular struggle ended with a Concord victory when Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos and his Acolyte, Veshra Kael, secured an alliance between the Concord and the Vorn Clan.

title: Cinder Wars
text: Battles, skirmishes, raids, and other actions continued for the next two years, with notable battles occurring on Veshtar, Velusia, Maldreth, and Tholos. During this time, the Severites developed various super weapons, including more traditional weapons such as the ion cannons of the battleship Malevolence, as well as biological weapons such as a variant of the Blue Shadow Virus. Meanwhile, the Concord launched several key offensives, including the Second Battle of Karnak, which obliterated Karnak' battle mechan foundries, and a failed Sephari-led operation to capture Supreme Commander of the Mechan Army General Skarl at Saleucami. Amidst the escalating conflict, many planets—including Korvan and other members of the Council of Neutral Systems—struggled to maintain their neutrality, but found it difficult to escape the carnage.

title: Cinder Wars
text: Over a year into the war, Concord Delegate Sennra Velora and Severite Delegate Mina Bonteri collaborated on an initiative to end the fighting. However, their collaboration ended after Maren and Skarl' bombing of the Concord capital on Velarion. Later, a peace conference on Korvan also failed to resolve the conflict. With no end in sight, the Sephari worked with local militaries, including Aqualis's military and Tessari's Naari Grand Army, and covertly trained an insurgent ashen cell to retake Veldoran from Severite occupation. Similarly, the Secession relied upon factions such as the Umbaran Militia and the Korvix Slave Dominion. Furthermore, a proxy war materialized when Mother Veska and her son, the now rogue Vorlan Lord Threnn, strove to exact their revenge on both the Vorlan and the Sephari.

title: Cinder Wars
text: During the war's third and final year, the Concord drove the Severites into redoubts within the Far Verge Territories, initiating a campaign termed the Far Verge Sieges. In an effort to reverse the course of the war, Skarl launched a massive strike on Velarion through the Deep Core. Much of the Confederate fleet was lost in the assault, along with Head of State Count Maren. The Secession quickly lost its core leadership in quick succession, with Skarl subsequently falling in battle during the Battle of Velkoth, and the Severite Council being massacred on Cindara. This, coupled with the issuing of Directive Null and the deactivation of the mechan army, led to the total capitulation of the Secession and, with it, an end to the war.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text:
# Davtherin Korrin Solvane

Davtherin Korrin Solvane, otherwise known as Dav Solvane, was a human smuggler, gambler, and entrepreneur who became Baron Administrator of Mist Spire and, later, a general in the Ashen Alliance. Born on Soltari, he was the owner of the Stormhawk before losing it to Rourke Caldris in a game of skarrn on Numidian Prime. Afterward, Solvane put an end to his days as a smuggler and became an entrepreneur, setting up a small mining operation on the planet Vedros before eventually becoming the leader of Mist Spire in the skies of the planet Velhaven.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text: During the Astral Civil War, Mourn Velgor arrived on Mist Spire to lay a trap for his son, Joran Drellos. As part of the trap, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan forced Solvane into tricking a group of Ashen, including Caldris and Princess Mira Vantar, leading them to Velgor himself. Though Velgor promised to leave Mist Spire without an Dominar presence, Solvane felt the deal had been altered to the point where he could no longer tolerate it. Solvane alerted his citizens to the Astral Dominion's presence and impending occupation and ordered an evacuation. He helped the Ashen try to rescue Caldris, who had been frozen in cryo-resin, from Borvad Kane, but the bounty hunter escaped.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text: Solvane joined the Ashen Alliance and set out to find Caldris. After locating him in the palace of Grobba the Vorn on Korrath, Solvane aided in his rescue. The Ashen returned to the fleet, and Solvane became a general, volunteering to lead the assault on the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station during the Battle of Velnar. During the battle, he piloted the Stormhawk into the battle station's core, firing the shot which destroyed it.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text: In the years of peace after the Dominion's dissolution, Solvane started a family and fathered a daughter named Kadara Solvane. However, while she was only an infant, his daughter was kidnapped by the Crimson Pact. Six years later, he embarked on a quest to the desert planet of Velsaan with Joran Drellos to find answers about the growing darkness in the Synth Flux, but failed to uncover anything. Seeking to bury the pain of those memories, Solvane settled on Velsaan and led a solitary lifestyle where he was known as the " Hermit " to the Aki-Aki of the Lurch Canyon. He lived alone for some years while keeping contact with the Caldris family and was later asked by Vantar's Defiance for his aid in the war against the Crimson Pact.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text:
In 35 AVR, Dav helped the Defiance and reunited with his old friend, Wrentak. Solvane played one more role in the fight for galactic freedom as he brought an assembled Citizens' Fleet to reinforce the Defiance at the battle at Vauldor, from which the Defiance emerged victorious.

## Biography

### Deals and adventures

A member of the tragic Solvane family, Davtherin Korrin Solvane, otherwise known as "Dav" Solvane, was born on the planet Soltari. During his youth, he became a smuggler and a gambler, excelling in a card game known as skarrn. He traveled throughout the galaxy and piloted a freighter called the Stormhawk, which he won through a game of skarrn at the gas giant Velhaven. The ship saved his life on numerous occasions. Sometime before 10 BVR, Dav won a subtropical moon in the Oseon Belt during a game of skarrn. Dav also developed a partnership with L3-37, a custom self-made piloting mechan.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text: During his time with L3, Dav nearly lost her to a Vorn after making a bad bet in a game of skarrn on Gonda. At one point, Solvane was involved in an incident with a Dawinian and their companion. He also came to meet the Vennika sisters, even showing Brea Vennika how to work the controls on the Stormhawk. At another point, Brea and Senni Vennika made a mess of the room they were staying in on the city-world of Velarion in order to get back at Solvane. At some point, Solvane met a mechan mechanic who worked on the Mid Verge planet Korvis, with that mechanic coming to owe Solvane a favor.

title: Davtherin Korrin Solvane
text: Sometime prior to the Battle of Drenn, Dav and L3-37 were ambushed in the Halthor sector when an Dominar interdictor dropped out from riftspace. As a result of the ambush, Solvane lost a majority of his shipment of walkers that he acquired from an Er'Kit arms dealer in the Noonian sector. Dav also had dealings with Scarlet Veil on Velusia. He completed his debt to Scarlet Veil and its leader, Varek Salin. At another point, Solvane visited Pantora and successfully convinced Dominar Vice Grand Administrator Prita Sven to let him leave the planet with a freighter full of poached forlyn carcasses.

title: Dovan Krell
text:
# Dovan Krell

Dovan Krell was a revered Synth Flux-sensitive human male Sephari Master and member of the Sephari High Council during the last years of the Concord Era. During his time in the Sephari Order, he once served as an elected leader of the Sephari and, during the Cinder Wars, as a Sephari General in The Grand Army of the Concord. He was the greatest champion of The Sephari Order and promoted its ancient traditions amidst the growing influence of the Umbra of the Synth Flux in the corrupt, declining days of the Concord.

title: Dovan Krell
text: During a mission to Metagos, Krell went by the pseudonym Solver. When the Severite Crisis spawned the birth of the League of Severed Worlds and sparked the Cinder Wars, Krell and the Sephari rallied to the defense of the Concord and became the leaders of the Grand Army of the Concord. Throughout the war, Krell served the Sephari and the Concord in various capacities—on the battlefield in command of the vatborn army, on Velarion as an overseer of the war effort and an advisor to Supreme Praetor Velran Castigon, and even as a diplomat to contested worlds, despite his disdain of politics. His exploits on the frontline served as a reminder of his reputation as a renowned Sephari warrior.

title: Dovan Krell
text: As the war drew to a close, Krell became increasingly suspicious of the praetor's motives, as Castigon had amassed near-dictatorial control over the Astral Conclave, and sensed the rising power of the Umbra in the galaxy. His suspicions were confirmed when Kaivan Drellos, a Sephari Knight and the Fated One of ancient prophecy, discovered that Castigon was Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan who manipulated and deceived the Concord and the Severite Alliance into war. Krell, along with Sephari Masters Kit Fisto, Saesee Tiin, and Agen Kolar, confronted Castigon with the intention of arresting him. Instead, the Dark Lord attacked them, striking them down one by one until only Krell was left. Krell bested Castigon in the confrontation and—deciding the praetor was too dangerous to be left alive due to his influence over the government—prepared to strike him down, but Kaivan Drellos intervened and betrayed Krell, allowing the Vorlan Lord to kill Krell

title: Dovan Krell
text: . Drellos had fallen to the temptation of the Umbra and became known as Mourn Velgor.

title: Dovan Krell
text:
Krell's actions led Castigon to deceitfully brand the Sephari as traitors to the Concord. The praetor executed Directive Null, forcing the vatborn troopers across the galaxy to turn against and kill their Sephari leaders, marking the fall of the Sephari Order and severites. Castigon transformed the Concord into the Astral Dominion and the Overlord's new regime promoted anti-Sephari sentiment across the galaxy. Through propaganda, the Dominion portrayed Krell as the leader of a criminal gang of Sephari who caused the outbreak of the Cinder Wars. In spite of the propaganda, some of Krell's actions were remembered with fondness; General Varlo Velko, who served alongside Krell during the Battle of Veshtar, remembered Krell with great respect and told the tale of how Krell helped him liberate Veshtar in a battle that earned Krell the name " The Hammer of Veshtar."

## Biography

### Early life

title: Dovan Krell
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Dovan Krell was born on the planet Haruun Kal in the year 72 BVR as a child of the most powerful members of his tribe. Like most other toddlers from Haruun Kal, Krell received an inoculation that left a small scar on his body. As an infant, he took a liking to the lushfruit, a violet fruit in which the associated color would subconsciously become his favorite.

title: Dovan Krell
text: A year after his birth, his parents were ambushed by garu-bears and his mother placed him in a high tree for safety. Both parents were killed in the ensuring conflict but Dovan was rescued by other warriors nearby, noted for his lack of grief from having unintentionally tapped into the Synth Flux, resulting in him being unusually calm. Although the warrior were unaware of why, they found the ordeal odd. Orphaned, the tribe is later visited by a Sephari whom happened upon Krell after hearing of his parent's brutal end and "strangeness" from the tribe, concluding possible force sensitivity. His tribe invokes a ancient ritual of choosing to decide his fate which included a lushfruit, a puzzle pyramid, and the shell of a plasma-brand. Krell ultimately chose the plasma-brand shell.

title: Dovan Krell
text: Due to his natural affinity of the Synth Flux and with his tribe's support, Krell was sent to the Sephari Order—a monastic order of protectors, sworn to defend the Astral Concord, and known as the guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy—to learn the Sephari arts. Krell never responded well to Grand Master Oodran's sense of humor. As a novice, he was taught to "let go" and trust in the Synth Flux. He also came to believe he was abandoned by his parents.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text:
# Grobba Vornak Sarr

Grobba Vornak Sarr, more commonly referred to as Grobba the Vorn or simply Grobba, and formally styled as His Excellency Grobba Vornak Sarr of Vornholt, Eminence of Korrath, was a Vorn male gangster and crime lord, as well as a leading member of the Grand Vorn Council and influential leader of the Vorn Clan, who operated and led a criminal empire from his palace on the Far Verge world of Korrath. Grobba was a major figure on Korrath, where he controlled the bulk of the piracy, slavery, and trafficking in illegal goods that generated most of the planet's wealth. He was also highly influential in the entire Far Verge as one of its most powerful crime lords.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text: During the Cinder Wars, Grobba's influence and power over the Far Verge, specifically its hyperlanes, was sought by both the Astral Concord and the League of Severed Worlds, who both courted Grobba's approval. When Brugo, Grobba's son, was kidnapped, the crime lord promised his support to whoever returned his son. When the Severites were revealed to have orchestrated Brugo's kidnapping, Grobba pledged his support to the Concord.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text: Grobba continued to operate in the Far Verge after the end of the Cinder Wars and the rise of the Astral Dominion, preserving his power base, despite the interference of Mourn Sarnex, the Astral Overlord. After the destruction of the Void Core by the Ashen Alliance, the Overlord sent Mourn Velgor to negotiate a deal with Grobba to secure raw materials for Dominar military production. Grobba's alliance with the Dominion allowed him and the Vorns to resist the Dominar crackdown against criminal elements in the Far Verge, as well as rid the Vorn of his competitors.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text:
After the smuggler Rourke Caldris failed to repay him for lost cargo, Grobba placed a high price on his head. Caldris was eventually delivered to him by one of his bounty hunters, Borvad Kane, as a gift from Mourn Velgor. However, this capture brought him to the attention of Sephari Knight Joran Drellos, who sought to rescue his friend from Grobba's imprisonment. As he attempted to execute the Sephari and his allies in the Great Pit of Varrok, Grobba was choked to death by Mira Vantar. With the Vorns unable to decide who would inherit Grobba's criminal ventures, many of his slaves, including the Niktos, were free, and his palace was occupied by his former Majordomo Vorel Talreq, who took his place as Warlord of Korrath until Kane killed and usurped him. Kane sought to rebuild Grobba's criminal empire in his own image, intending to rule with respect rather than the fear that the Vorn instilled in his followers.

## Biography

### Korrath Crime Lord

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text:
## Biography

### Korrath Crime Lord

Grobba Vornak Sarr was a Vorn who hailed from Vornholt. He was born in 600 BVR. He was the grandson of Mama and Papa the Vorns, and the nephew of Zorto and Ebor, as they were the siblings of his father. His mother left enough of a mark on him that, years later, he would force the Askajian dancer Yarna d'al' Gargan to wear special makeup to make her look more like his genitrix. He also had a cousin named Crakka and a nephew named Gorga.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text: Several centuries before the Astral Civil War, he became the reigning crime lord in the Far Verge, owning several criminal enterprises which included smuggling, glitterstim glimmerdust dealing, slave trading, assassination and piracy. At some point, Grobba became affiliated with the Vexmora Syndicate. As a result of his collaboration with the Vexmora, he gained a position on the Grand Vorn Council. As a crime lord, Grobba based his illicit operation out of his palace in the Northern Dune Sea of the desert world Korrath, from where he spread his operations and influence across the Far Verge by employing a network of smugglers who moved his goods across the galaxy.

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text:
Forming a powerful criminal empire, his operations grew to include slavery, arms dealing, glimmerdust smuggling, and gambling. Gambling was a prominent feature of the Krevar Hollow Grand Arena, where Grobba controlled the gambling and concessions during the popular podraces. The glimmerdust trade was a major part of Grobba's empire, becoming one of the primary ways the Vorn made money. To those who respected his authority, very few, he was formally styled as "His Excellency Grobba Vornak Sarr of Vornholt, Eminence of Korrath."

### The High Concord

title: Grobba Vornak Sarr
text:
### The High Concord

Years before the Great Disaster, Grobba, along with other Vorns, attended a banquet on Hynestia as part of a treaty negotiation between the Hynestian royal family and the Grand Vorn Council. The Vorns planted Povo Punch in the drink menu as a means of inciting a diplomatic incident. When Sephari Master Lynela Kabe-Oyu, Stellan Gios, and his acolyte Vernestra Rwoh, noticed the Povo Punch and attempted to save the Vorns, the Vorns opened fire on the banquet, claiming that the incident was an insult that justified violent action against Hynestia.

After the Sephari settled the situation, Grobba and his fellow Vorns attempted to escape, only to be stopped by the Sephari themselves. Queen Nyla, Ruler of Hynestia, stepped in to officially capture Grobba and his fellow Vorn conspirators for attempting to disrupt the treaty and to assassinate attendees of the diplomatic banquet, putting him for ransom to the Vorn Council.

title: Jaren Kane
text:
# Jaren Kane

Jaren Kane was a famed Korvanic human male bounty hunter and the vatborn template of the Grand Army of the Concord. Known as the best bounty hunter in the galaxy during the final years of the Astral Concord, Kane was proficient in marksmanship as well as unarmed combat. The Korvanic armor that he wore featured various weapons and gadgets, including a flamethrower, dual WESTAR-34 pulse-caster pistols, and a jetpack. His personal starship was the Vornclaw-31 -class patrol and attack craft Slave I.

title: Jaren Kane
text: Hailing from the planet Concord Dawn, Kane was a foundling of the Korvanics trained by a mentor known partially as Jaste, and, as a Korvanic warrior, fought in the Korvanic Civil Wars before becoming a bounty hunter. As a bounty hunter, Kane worked with and became acquainted with several fellow hunters and individuals in the criminal underworld including the Velmari Rezz Drannor, whom Kane once mentored, Nyx Vale, Tarsa Brixx, and the infamous pirate Brakka Varn. In time, Kane became widely regarded as the galaxy's best bounty hunter, with a notoriety matched by few other bounty hunters.

title: Jaren Kane
text: Shortly after the Invasion of Tessari, the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sevrin hired Kane to serve as the genetic foundation of an army secretly bred on the Wildreach world of Tholos. His DNA spawned millions of vatborn troopers who shared his face, voice, and were trained to become soldiers. As part of his payment, Kane was given an unaltered vatborn whom he raised as his son, Borvad Kane. In the last days of the Severite Crisis, Kane was involved in the failed plot to assassinate Delegate Sennra Velora on Velarion. The Sephari Order investigated the incident, forcing Kane to leave the Tholosian homeworld after he was confronted by Sephari Knight Orven Taskorr.

title: Jaren Kane
text:
Taskorr tracked Kane to Karnak where he discovered the bounty hunter's connection with Count Maren and the League of Severed Worlds. Kane fought against the Sephari assault team during the First Battle of Karnak, and was beheaded by Sephari Master Dovan Krell in 22 BVR. His legacy survived not only through the millions of vatborn troopers that formed the backbone of the Concord Military, but also Borvad, who became a bounty hunter like his father before him. By the era of the Astral Dominion, Borvad possessed the same set of Korvanic armor worn by Jaren, although its appearance had been altered significantly.

## Biography

### Early life

title: Jaren Kane
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Jaren Kane was born in 66 BVR and was from the Korvanic colony planet Concord Dawn, a world within the Korvan sector of the Far Verge Territories. Although he told others he came from this Korvanic world, his exact history remained unknown, much to Kane's enjoyment. As a boy, Kane was a prodigy in unarmed combat. Following the murder of his parents, Kane was found on Concord Dawn by and taken into ranks of the Korvanics as a foundling. The legendary warriors raised him to become a Korvanic warrior. He was taught by a mentor known partially as Jaste.

title: Jaren Kane
text:
Kane participated in the Korvanic Civil Wars, and it was during the wars that he was first given his own set of distinctive Korvanic armor. Eventually, however, his time with the Korvanics led him to pursue a career as a bounty hunter. Although he would retain his Korvanic armor, Prime Minister Almec of the New Korvanics disavowed any connection to Kane, claiming that he was simply a bounty hunter who had somehow stolen an artifact from Korvan's troubled past.

### Rise of Jaren Kane

title: Jaren Kane
text:
### Rise of Jaren Kane

During the final years of the Astral Concord, but still many years prior to the Invasion of Tessari, Kane, over time, rose to the top of the bounty hunting trade, where he expertly used his advanced armor and twin pulse-caster pistols to hunt down fugitives. Initially, Kane was not able to just take on the jobs that he wanted, and it took him many years to build his reputation until he could operate as he chose to and saw fit. Ultimately, Kane became widely regarded as the best bounty hunter in the galaxy. At some point in his career Kane began to work with Tarsa Brixx as a frequent accomplice. Kane was also an associate of pirate captain Brakka Varn and fellow bounty hunter Nyx Vale. Once being mentored by the legendary man, Rezz Drannor, a Velmari who was a major bounty hunter by the time of the Cinder Wars, came to owe Kane several favors that he never paid off.

title: Jaren Kane
text: At one point in time, Kane and Brixx journeyed to a terrestrial astronomical object called Snugano. While there, Kane and Brixx used a tactic, with his companion nearly dying using her abilities as a Clawdite to morph into a fur-covered beast. At another point, Kane undertook another job to Oovo 4, a prison moon that Vornclaw attack craft were used to guard. During this event, Kane stole a Vornclaw-31 starship, naming it Slave I, utilizing it as his personal transport, and upgrading the craft extensively, outfitting the vessel with a number of weapons, including laser cannons, projectile launchers, and seismic charges.

title: Joran Drellos
text:
# Joran Drellos

Joran Drellos, a Synth Flux-sensitive human male, was a legendary Sephari Master who fought in the Astral Civil War during the reign of the Astral Dominion. Along with his companions, Princess Mira Vantar and General Rourke Caldris, Drellos served as a revolutionary on the side of the Alliance to Restore the Concord—an organization committed to the downfall of the Astral Dominion and the restoration of democracy. Following the war, Drellos became a living legend, and was remembered as one of the greatest Sephari in galactic history.

title: Joran Drellos
text: The son of Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos and Delegate Sennra Velora, Joran Drellos was born along with his twin sister, Mira, in 19 BVR. As a result of Velora's death and Kaivan's fall to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, the Drellos children were separated and sent into hiding, with Mira adopted by the royal family of Aurelia while Joran was raised by his relatives on Korrath. Longing for a life of adventure and purpose, Drellos joined the Insurrection and began learning the ways of the Synth Flux under the guidance of Sephari Master Orven Taskorr, whose first apprentice was Joran's own father. During the Battle of Drenn, Drellos saved the Alliance from annihilation by destroying the Dominion's planet-killing superweapon, the Void Core. He continued his training in the years that followed, determined to become a Sephari Knight like his father before him, and found a new mentor in Grand Master Oodran

title: Joran Drellos
text: . After his master's death, Drellos participated in the Battle of Velnar in 4 AVR, during which he confronted the Vorlan Lord Mourn Velgor, whom he learned was in fact his father, Kaivan Drellos. With Joran's help, Kaivan returned to the Lumen of the Synth Flux by killing the Overlord and Dark Lord of the Vorlan Mourn Sarnex at the cost of his own life, fulfilling his destiny as the Fated One. Following the Battle of Velnar, Drellos trained his sister as a first Sephari apprentice on Ajan Kloss, but Mira ended her training after the birth of her son and seeing his death as a result of finishing her knighthood.

title: Joran Drellos
text: With the Vorlan's destruction and the subsequent capitulation of the Dominion, Drellos became a living legend as he traveled across the galaxy during New Concord Era, searching for knowledge that would aid him in rebuilding the Sephari Order, and serving the New Concord and its allies where he could. As the war raged for a year after Velnar, Drellos was heavily involved with the New Concord's efforts against self-declared Grand Warden Ubrik Adelhard in the Vandel sector, before defeating the madman at the Battle of Drava. Around 6 AVR, Drellos committed himself to the liberation of the Nagai and their homeworld Nagi from beneath the heel of their enslavers. Later, in 9 AVR, Drellos rescued Yobi, a Korvanic Synth Flux-sensitive child that belonged to the same species as Oodran, from Warden Veskar's forces, and after temporarily taking the child as an apprentice on Ossus

title: Joran Drellos
text: . # Kaivan Drellos

Kaivan Drellos was a legendary Synth Flux-sensitive human male who was a Sephari Knight of the Astral Concord and the prophesied Fated One of the Sephari Order, destined to bring balance to the Synth Flux. Also known as " Ani " during his childhood, Drellos earned the moniker " Hero With No Fear " from his accomplishments in the Cinder Wars. His alter ego, Mourn Velgor, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan, was created when Drellos turned to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, pledging his allegiance to the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex at the end of the Concord Era.

title: Kaivan Drellos
text: A vergence in the Synth Flux, Kaivan Drellos was born on the desert planet of Korrath in the Far Verge Territories in 41 BVR. He was the son of Mella Drellos, a slave who conceived a child without a father. His blood contained over twenty-thousand synth-nodes, surpassing Grand Master Oodran and all other Sephari in the galaxy. Veyron Dask, the Sephari Master who discovered Drellos during the Invasion of Tessari in 32 BVR, theorized that Drellos was conceived by the synth-nodes. Following the Battle of Tessari, the Sephari High Council admitted Kaivan Drellos into the Order as the Acolyte of Sephari Knight Orven Taskorr despite feeling that he was too old and emotional to adhere to the Sephari Code. Drellos remained a Acolyte through the beginning of the Cinder Wars, instigated by events set in motion by Count Maren. Although Sephari doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Kaivan Drellos had a secret wife, Delegate Sennra Velora of Tessari

title: Kaivan Drellos
text: . Although Sephari doctrine prohibited romantic relationships, Kaivan Drellos had a secret wife, Delegate Sennra Velora of Tessari. After receiving his knighthood, Drellos oversaw the Sephari training of his own apprentice, Veshra Kael. By 19 BVR, when Kael walked away from the Sephari Order, Drellos began to struggle with feelings of failure towards his apprentice and the Order itself.

title: Kaivan Drellos
text: Following the death of Count Maren during the Battle of Velarion, Kaivan Drellos's faith in the Sephari was further shaken when he was put on the Sephari Council without the rank of master. He also learned that Supreme Praetor Velran Castigon was Mourn Sarnex, the elusive Dark Lord of the Vorlan who orchestrated the war in order to take over the galaxy. title: Kaivan Drellos
text: Being the Overlord's Fist and later being elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Dominar fleet, Velgor enforced the rule of the New Order as the Overlord's Vorlan apprentice throughout most of the Dominar Era and was thus seen as de facto Commander-in-Chief of the entire Dominar Military. # Karnak

Karnak, referred to as Karnessa by some natives, was the desert home planet of the Karnaki. It hosted the League of Severed Worlds major battle mechan foundries and was the site of the First Battle of Karnak, the opening conflict of the Cinder Wars, as well as the subsequent invasion by the Astral Concord. During and after the war, the Void Core was constructed above the planet. Five years after the conflict's conclusion and transformation of the Astral Concord, the Astral Dominion would garrison the planet heavily and attempt to mine the planet's asteroids for minerals. At least five years after the Cinder Wars, the Dominion moved the Void Core to another construction site and the planet was sterilized by the Dominion as a security measure, an act which resulted in the virtual elimination of the planet's native population.

## Description

title: Karnak
text:
## Description

Situated in the Karnak system of the Arkanis sector in the Far Verge Territories, the planet of Karnak was 43,000 light years from the Astral Core, and less than a parsec away from the neighboring Far Verge planet of Korrath. It was the homeworld of the Karnaki, a species of sentient insectoids. It had a breathable atmosphere, but a hot and arid climate. Its irradiated surface was covered in harsh, rocky deserts, marked by mesas and buttes. Both its rocks and sky were tinted in shades of red. Surface water was scarce, amounting to only 5% of the entire total planetary surface. However, Karnak had frequent flash floods. From space, it could be seen that Karnak had awe-inspiring rocky rings. The planet was orbited by fifteen moons, four of which were major and included the icy moon of Bahryn.

## History

### Ancient history

title: Karnak
text:
## History

### Ancient history

At some point in the ancient history of Karnak, a comet crashed in one of the planet's many moons. The collision debris not only formed the famous rings of Karnak, but also formed a field of small asteroids which would sometimes rain down on the planet's surface.

### Under the Concord

title: Karnak
text:
### Under the Concord

Astral colonizers were attracted to Karnak when the Korr system was discovered due to its close proximity to Korrath. When the Astral Concord made first contact with the Karnaki, it was successful and beneficial to both groups. Due to this, the Karnaki became interested with Concord technology and became skilled in adapting and improving advanced technology. As such, Karnaki exported mechans and other technology to the rest of the galaxy, although this didn't last long. Once Korrath was almost abandoned by the first wave of colonizers, Karnak suffered from its distance from the Core Systems as visitors to the planet grew smaller and smaller until visitors stopped traveling to Karnak altogether. Karnaki exports were more easily met by other manufacturers closer to the Core.

title: Karnak
text:
Karnaki became split over the idea of working with offworlders, and with the planet's economy in ruins, wars erupted throughout the planet for millennia, while the rest of the galaxy largely forgot the planet and left it to its endless wars. A few hundred years prior to the Severite Crisis, the world was rediscovered by the Astral Concord and manufacturing deals were made to sell and distribute their advanced technology and mechans. Allying with the Forgeworks Corporation of the Forge Union, the Karnaki Hives produced protocol mechans, battle mechans, and labor mechans in concert with Forgeworks for centuries.

### The Cinder Wars

title: Karnak
text: In the later years of the Astral Concord, Karnak became a major base of operations for the League of Severed Worlds, a collection of star systems that spread across the galaxy. The enormous Karnaki mechan factories began to manufacture of tens of thousands of different types of battle mechans, thus maintaining their own Karnaki mechan army. During that time, Karnak built mechan armies for large corporations such as the Commerce League. To produce the Combine's mechan armies, Forgeworks Armor Workshop had approached the Karnaki on the Combine's behalf with the offer for Karnak to establish mechan foundries, create battle mechans, and produce other automata.
