title: Korrath
text:
# Korrath

Korrath was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy's Far Verge Territories. Part of a binary star system, the planet orbited two scorching suns, resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms. The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Skrit and Dune Stalker species and of Kaivan and Joran Drellos, who would go on to shape galactic history.

title: Korrath
text: It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers, which were later used by the Skrit population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Vorn Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

title: Korrath
text: Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Korrath gained the notice of the Astral Dominion during the Astral Civil War when an escape pod carrying two mechans in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Far Verge world. The Dominion went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Grobba Vornak Sarr of the Vorn Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Dominion and a Ashen Alliance cell on Korrath that culminated in a battle that left the Dominion's hold on the world significantly weakened.

title: Korrath
text:
Following the death of Grobba and the withdrawal of Dominar forces after the Battle of Velnar, an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Borvad Kane returned and took over Grobba's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Vorn Clan and the Vexil Syndicate, the new Warlord was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Korrath. With help from the Korvanic Vane Korrick, Kane rallied the denizens of the settlements Krevar Hollow and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

## Description

title: Korrath
text:
## Description

Korrath was a hot desert planet located in the Far Verge, a region of the galaxy far removed from its core. It had three moons, Ghomrassen, Guermessa, and Chenini. Korrath orbited twin suns, Korr I and Korr II. According to Skrit folklore, the desert known as the Dune Sea was once a true ocean. The whole planet was covered in harsh deserts, and only a small part of its northern hemisphere could sustain intelligent life. The landscape was covered with sand dunes, mountains, and canyons, which made traversing the planet very difficult. Due to the absence of surface water, those who lived on Korrath had to draw moisture through the dry air.

title: Korrath
text:
Rain was incredibly rare on Korrath, coming once a year, decade, or century. When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species, the largest of which were the carnivorous krayt dragons. The common krayt dragon, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater krayt dragon, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common durga and eopie species also found a home on the world, along with dewbacks, rontos, womp rats, massiffs, and scurriers.

The cities of Korrath were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living.

## History

title: Korrath
text:
## History

### Early history

Korrath was the homeworld of the Skrit and Dune Stalker species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Lehon, Korrath had also been inhabited by a group called the Kumumgah during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Korrath's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

title: Korrthan
text:
# Korrthan

Korrthans, known in their own language of Korrthani as " the People of the Trees," were a species of tall, hairy humanoids that were native to the planet Verdara. A notable member of this species was the warrior Wrentak, Rourke Caldris's best friend and co- pilot, who played a vital role in the Cinder Wars during the Battle of Verdara, the Astral Civil War by aiding the Ashen Alliance in their fight against the Astral Dominion, and the war against the Crimson Pact. They were quite strong, and were known to rip people's arms out of their sockets when provoked. Though being from a temperate planet known for its swamps and forests, Korrthans were perfectly comfortable on icy worlds like Ilum and Brennix, not requiring any additional protective clothing, i.e. gloves or boots.

## Biology and appearance

title: Korrthan
text:
## Biology and appearance

Korrthans were a tall species of furry humanoids from the planet Verdara, who could grow to a height of nearly three meters. They were covered from head to toe in a thick, shaggy coat of hair with water-shedding properties that notably came in shades of brown, black, gray, and white. The species had two sexes, female and male. The latter grew long beards in adult life. The average male weighed 150 kilograms while the average female weighed 100 kilograms. The Korrthans' eye color ranged from blue to brown. Korrthans were big eaters, with the average adult requiring 3,500-6,000 calories a day of food. Their diet consisted of wild plants, berries, meat, and spices. They preferred their spices to be hot.

title: Korrthan
text: While Korrthans did not like eating blosphi extract, it provided them with enough nutrition to survive. The " Korrthan flu " was a sickness that affected Korrthans. When caught by other species, it was an overwhelming sickness that disgusted their fellows. The literary collective term for Korrthans was a grove of Korrthans. Many of their kind were known to understand Astral Basic but were unable to speak it due to their species' vocal structure.

title: Korrthan
text: Korrthans had extendable claws which they used for climbing; using them for anything else violated the Korrthan honor code. Despite their fearsome appearance and volatile temperament, Korrthans were regarded as intelligent, sophisticated, loyal and trusting. When angered, Korrthans were known to descend into a berserker rage. Korrthans had an average lifespan of 400 standard years, and they appeared not to age over a span of fifty years. Their lifespans dramatically decreased due to the harsh working conditions in the glimmerdust mines of Drungar. During their prime growing years, Korrthans were often hungry, forcing them to eat whenever they could. One Korrthan, Lohgarra, lived healthily for centuries—the only distinction being her white fur.

title: Korrthan
text:
They could learn to understand other languages, like Astral Basic Standard, but they were physically unable to speak them due to their strange vocal chords that prevented them from speaking verbal languages. To those who had not learned to understand Korrthani, the Korrthan language, it appeared they spoke in a series of growls and purrs. Although a rare phenomenon, Synth Flux-sensitive Korrthans were possible, and some joined the ranks of the Sephari, becoming a source of great pride for their people. Such Korrthans included the Sephari Master Kelnacca, Sephari Master Arkoff, Sephari Knight Burryaga Agaburry, Sephari Master Tyvokka, and the novice Gungi.

## History

### The Cinder Wars

title: Korrthan
text:
## History

### The Cinder Wars

Korrthans originated on the Mid Verge forest planet of Verdara. In the ancient past, they invented and crafted weapons that fired poisoned darts and arrows. During the Cinder Wars and the reign of King Grakchawwaa, the Korrthans remained fiercely loyal to the Astral Concord and fought alongside them in several star systems. Towards the end of the conflict, Korrthan forces also defended their homeworld from a Severite invasion with the help of Astral Concord forces led by Sephari Master Oodran, who had good relations with them.

### Age of the Dominion

title: Korrthan
text:
### Age of the Dominion

At the end of the Cinder Wars, numerous Korrthans were slaughtered by the vatborn troopers they allied with in the ensuing chaos of the anti-Sephari Order 66, and soon after the establishment of the Astral Dominion, their homeworld of Verdara was blockaded by the Dominion. The Age of the Dominion saw the softening and repeal of anti- slavery laws, which ultimately led to the Dominion classifying the Korrthans as non-sentient. The Dominion enslaved the Korrthans not because they were a meaningful threat to the Dominion but because their massive, robust physiology allowed them to work long and hard in extreme conditions.

title: Korrthan
text: As a result, many Korrthans were enslaved and made to build much of the Dominar war machine, sent to be worked to death in the dangerous glimmerdust mines of the planet Drungar, or on construction sites such as the Void Core, though a number escaped this fate. Numerous Korrthans were bred for use in medical experimentation, and some were used as playthings for Grand Warden Lozen Tolruck, Dominar governor of Verdara, who occasionally hunted live Korrthans for sport.

title: Korvanic
text:
# Korvanic

The Korvanics—known in Mando'a as the Mando'ade (" Children of Korvan ")—were a clan-based culture composed of members from multiple species and bound by a common creed, language, and code. Known primarily as highly-effective mercenaries and bounty hunters, Korvanics as a socio-cultural group have at various points in galactic history played a major role as legendary warriors and conquerors.

Originating around the year 9991 BVR on the planet of Korvan in the galaxy's Far Verge Territories, the Korvanics' way of life revolved around honor and war, being led by a sole ruler known as the Korvex, whose Protectors maintained a relative state of peace and unity between their people's warrior clans. As a result of their warrior culture, the Korvanics launched several wars of expansion by the time of the Old Concord-era, colonizing nearby worlds such as Krownest, Ordo, and Concord Dawn, leading the sector surrounding their homeworld to be known as Korvanic Space.

title: Korvanic
text:
Throughout their history, several prominent groups of Korvanic warriors came into existence, such as Korvanic crusaders, rally masters, and Korvanic Neo-Crusaders, all of whom waged war on the Astral Concord and the Sephari Order. According to legends, many of these conflicts involved a Korvex who went by the name of Korvan the Great.

In spite of this, relations between the Korvanics and the Sephari were not always hostile, as Tarre Kraddok, a human Korvanic, was inducted into the Sephari Order as a child, creating a plasma-brand known as the Voidblade around the year 1050 BVR. Tarre eventually founded House Kraddok, claiming the position of Korvex, with the Voidblade becoming a symbol of leadership for both House Kraddok and the Korvanic people as a whole.

title: Korvanic
text: However, after Kraddok's death, members of his house raided the Sephari Temple during the fall of the Old Concord, stealing the Voidblade and using it to reunify the Korvanic people, waging war once more on the Sephari Order. Unfortunately, the final conflict between the Korvanic warlords and the Sephari at the planet Korvan led to a cataclysm that turned much of its surface into a lifeless white desert, rendering it uninhabitable outside of hermetically sealed dome cities. After their defeat, the Korvanics remained isolated in their sector well into the High Concord Era, not attempting to wage another war on either the Sephari or the Concord, with which they coexisted through treaties. However, the Korvanics' warrior ways and desire for conquest remained alive, eventually leading to infighting and civil wars.

title: Korvanic
text: However, although Korvan was still under control of traditional Korvanic warriors, much of the planet's population had become part of a pacifist movement known as the New Korvanics, led by the young Duchess Arene Vael of House Vael, with the traditionalist warriors being forced to use violence to hold on to power. Eventually, around the year 42 BVR, a civil war broke out between the pacifist New Korvanic movement and the martial traditionalists, who wished to maintain their warrior heritage. Korvan's capital of Keldabe was destroyed during the Korvanic Civil War, and many perished during the conflict, including Duke Adonai Vael, Arene's father. Arene herself had to remain under protection from the Sephari Order, as the traditionalists sent bounty hunters after her. However, Korvan's traditionalist minority was eventually defeated during the war, being exiled to Korvan's moon of Concordia

title: Korvanic
text: . However, Korvan's traditionalist minority was eventually defeated during the war, being exiled to Korvan's moon of Concordia. While the Iron Watch, a traditionalist group under Korvex Korin Kraddok, wished to retake their homeworld, the Old Korvanics scattered across the galaxy as mercenaries.

title: Korvanic
text: During the Cinder Wars, members of the warrior culture would align themselves with both sides of the conflict, which was secretly orchestrated by the Vorlan Order, who hired the Korvanic bounty hunter Jaren Kane to become the vatborn template for the Grand Army of the Concord, with Kane's vatborn being trained by the Korvanic Protectors, while the Iron Watch briefly joined the League of Severed Worlds, in hopes of reclaiming Korvan. Under the New Korvanic government, Korvan remained neutral and participated in the Council of Neutral Systems as a leading member. However thanks to being backed up by the criminal conglomerate known as the Shadow Collective, Iron Watch was able to topple the ruling New Korvanic regime, but the machinations of Threnn, leader of the Collective, led to another civil war among the Iron Watch, which split into the Collective-backed Korvanic super commandos, and the Korvan resistance, which was supported by the Concord

title: Korvanic
text: . However, the conflict culminated in the occupation of Korvan by the Astral Concord and its subsequent government, the Astral Dominion, while Concord Dawn, the Protectors' headquarters, was transformed into a protectorate.

title: Maren
text:
# Maren

Maren was a Synth Flux-sensitive human male Serennian who served as a Sephari Master during the waning years of the Astral Concord and later Count of House Valdoris. He became dissatisfied with the Sephari Order and fell to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, becoming the Dark Lord of the Vorlan Mourn Sevrin. After leaving the Sephari Order, he served as Count of Valdoris and Head of State of the League of Severed Worlds during the Cinder Wars. He was the second apprentice of Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan, whose plan to conquer the galaxy relied on Maren leading a pan- galactic secessionist movement against the Concord. As such, Maren immersed himself in the Umbra of the Synth Flux and worked tirelessly to advance his and his master's Grand Plan while being unaware that he was merely a pawn of his master.

title: Maren
text: Born in 102 BVR during the High Concord Era, Maren was taken by the Sephari Order after being abandoned by his family and learned the Sephari arts as the Acolyte of Oodran, the legendary Grand Master of the Sephari Order; he went on to take Voss Tarmin and the maverick Veyron Dask as his two Acolyte learners at different points, before eventually ascending to the Sephari Council. He went on to become a respected and legendary Sephari Master in his own right. A political idealist, the corruption in the Astral Conclave—as well as the traditions of the Sephari—disillusioned him. In 42 BVR Maren left the Order and returned to his homeworld, where he reclaimed his title of Count and heritage as a nobleman after overthrowing his corrupt brother, Ramil. His former peers believed his decision was misguided but still held him in high esteem. However the Count of Valdoris began to secretly conspire with Mourn Sarnex

title: Maren
text: . However the Count of Valdoris began to secretly conspire with Mourn Sarnex. After the death of Veyron Dask at the Battle of Tessari in 32 BVR, and following the duel in the Works which saw the death of Sephari Master Vossa, Maren embraced the Umbra and adopted the name of Mourn Sevrin upon fully becoming the apprentice of Mourn Sarnex. Throughout the first decade of Velran Castigon's chancellery, Maren used his resources and charisma to recruit entire star systems to the Severite cause. At the same time, he oversaw the development of two vast armies that would be pitted against each other in the conflict to come: the Severite Mechan Army, which consisted of battle mechans manufactured on worlds such as Karnak; and the Grand Army of the Concord, composed of vatborn troopers bred on Tholos and modeled on the bounty hunter Jaren Kane.

title: Maren
text: After years of maneuvering the galaxy into a state of war, the Cinder Wars began when the newly formed Concord Military invaded Karnak in 22 BVR. As leader of the Severites, Maren delegated military authority to a cadre of subordinates personally trained by himself, including General Skarl and Nyssa Vashka. While Skarl was trained only in the art of plasma-brand combat, Vashka was strong with the Synth Flux, affording her the opportunity to learn the ways of the Umbra from Maren. The Vorlan, however, remained faithful to Mourn Vorrane's Rule of Two; and as such, Maren was compelled to betray his disciple after Sarnex became suspicious of his own apprentice's intentions. Though he sought to replace Vashka with Vrenn Garokk and later Quinlan Salin, Maren ultimately remained beholden to his master's will, which would eventually be his undoing.

title: Maren
text:
By the third year of the war, Maren and Skarl succeeded in abducting Praetor Castigon (per Sarnex' plan) from the Concord capital of Velarion in 19 BVR. During the ensuing Battle of Velarion, he was confronted and defeated by the Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos, who summarily executed the Count via beheading at the Praetor's behest. In the days following Maren's death, Castigon revealed to the Sephari that he was, in fact, Mourn Sarnex, who betrayed his apprentice in order to replace him with the younger and more promising Drellos. With the subsequent fall of the Sephari Order, Sarnex consolidated his power upon declaring himself Overlord of the Astral Dominion, which Sevrin had an instrumental role in establishing. As for Drellos, he succeeded the late Mourn Sevrin as Sarnex' third and last apprentice, resulting in his transformation into Mourn Velgor and proving his slain victim's words of sensing fear, hate, and anger.

title: Maren
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Maren was born in 102 BVR during the High Concord Era, on the planet Valdoris to the planet's ruler, Count Valdor, and his wife, Countess Anya. The child's Synth Flux-sensitivity manifested itself rapidly, scaring his father, who hated and feared those he dismissed as "freaks." Valdor contacted the Sephari Order and told them to take his son. However, instead of waiting for the Sephari seekers to arrive, Valdor abandoned the infant outside his palace on the edges of the forest without clothes or any form of identification. A seeker rescued Maren before he froze to death or was eaten by spine-wolves, and brought the child to the Sephari Grand Temple on Velarion.

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text:
# Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris

Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris was a Synth Flux-sensitive human Aurelian female politician, Sephari, and military leader who served in the Alliance to Restore the Concord during the Dominar Era and the New Concord and Defiance in the subsequent New Concord Era. Shortly after birth on Volis Reach, she was adopted into the House of Vantar—the Aurelian royal family—and was raised as Princess Mira Vantar of Aurelia, a planet in the Core Systems known for its dedication to pacifism. The princess was raised as the daughter of Delegate Daro Veshar Vantar and his wife, Queen Dalia Vantar, making her the heir to the Aurelian monarchy. Instilled with the values of her adopted homeworld, Vantar devoted her life to the restoration of democracy by opposing authoritarian regimes, such as the Astral Dominion and the Crimson Pact.

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text: Born in 19 BVR as Mira Velora Drellos, she was the daughter of the Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos and Delegate Sennra Velora of Tessari. Her birth occurred in the aftermath of the Cinder Wars, which saw the Sephari Order purged and the Astral Concord reorganized into the Astral Dominion. With her mother's death in childbirth and her father's fall to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, Mira and her twin brother, Joran, were separated to keep them hidden from the hands of her father and the Overlord. As the adopted daughter of a politician, Mira grew up peacefully—albeit secluded—on Aurelia until she was kidnapped by mercenaries led by Vect Nokru—under the orders of the Third Sister, a member of the Tribunal—in 9 BVR. Since he had fought alongside her adoptive father in the Cinder Wars, Sephari Master Orven Taskorr went to Mira's rescue on Daiyu, and, after evading the Dominion's hand on Mapuzo and Jabiim, Mira was brought back to Aurelia

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text: . Years later, Mira succeeded Daro by representing their homeworld in the Dominar Conclave, though secretly she supported the Insurrection. During the Astral Civil War, however, Aurelia was destroyed along with its inhabitants and the royal family by the Dominion's DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, causing Vantar to openly fight the New Order as one of the Ashen Alliance’s substantial heroes.

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text: In the aftermath of the Battle of Velnar, Vantar married the Veltari smuggler Rourke Caldris and learned the Sephari arts as her brother's apprentice until giving birth to her son, Ben Caldris, on the day of the Dominion's capitulation in 5 AVR. Her personal and political life suffered in the years that followed, with Ben turning to the Umbra like his grandfather before him, adopting the persona of Vexen Korr, and the Astral Conclave sidelining Vantar's career. Adopting the military rank of general, she led the Defiance and their efforts to oppose the rising Crimson Pact during the Cold War while seeking to make amends with Ben in hopes that her son will return to the Lumen of the Synth Flux like her father during the Battle of Velnar. Despite her efforts, the Crimson Pact succeeded in destroying the New Concord, and Vantar's husband died at the hands of their estranged son in 34 AVR

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text: . Vantar continued to lead the Defiance during the war against the Crimson Pact, all the while passing on her Sephari training onto Sefa—a Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger from Drava and Joran’s apprentice.

title: Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris
text:
As her health declined, Vantar used her remaining strength to reach her son, calling him back to the Lumen. Following her death on Ajan Kloss in 35 AVR, her final actions inspired Sefa and the Defiance to defeat the forces of the reborn Mourn Sarnex's Vorlan Eternal on Vauldor and spark an uprising against the Crimson Pact across the galaxy. The heir to three inheritances, Mira Drellos Vantar Caldris's legacy passed on to the Sephari Sefa Drellos, the military leader Jax Rell of the Defiance, and Ben Caldris, her only child, who ultimately returned to the light before sacrificing his life for Sefa and becoming one with the Synth Flux to join his mother and the Drellos family.

## Biography

### Pre-birth

Toward the end of the Cinder Wars, a galactic conflict fought between the Astral Concord and the League of Severed Worlds that was engineered by the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex, Sephari Master Oodran set out on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality. His journey took him to Vaulmir, the ancient Vorlan homeworld, where he faced visions of the future. At the end of his journey, the Synth Flux Priestess, Serenity, who had guided his journey, told him that there was another Drellos, and Oodran heard his voice from the future say so as well. These events not only alluded to the potential he would sense in Mira, but to what Oodran would tell her twin brother, Joran, about Mira in his last words, before his death.

# Mourn Sarnex

Mourn Sarnex, born Velran Castigon and also simply known as the Overlord, was a male human Dark Lord of the Vorlan and Overlord of the Astral Dominion, with his reign lasting from 19 BVR to 4 AVR. Rising to power in the Astral Conclave as the delegate of Tessari, the secretive Vorlan Lord cultivated two identities, Sarnex and Castigon, using both to further his political career and deceive his way into accomplishing his goal. He orchestrated the fall of the Astral Concord and the Sephari Order through the Cinder Wars, and then established his reign over the galaxy which lasted until his death at the Battle of Velnar. However, the Umbra of the Synth Flux gave rise to powers which allowed him to escape death, seeking further immortality until the Overlord was eventually permanently destroyed and killed during the Battle of Vauldor by Sefa, his granddaughter born from his Strand-Cast vatborn son Dathan and his daughter-in-law Miramir.

title: Mourn Sarnex
text: Born on the Mid Verge planet Tessari in 84 BVR as the High Concord Era ended, Sarnex possessed a strong connection to the Synth Flux, and was secretly trained in the ways of the Vorlan by Mourn Veshk. He eventually betrayed and killed his Vorlan Master, in order to train his own Vorlan apprentice, Mourn Threnn, for the Rule of Two limited their ranks to two Vorlan Lords at any given time. As a result of the Invasion of Tessari, a crisis orchestrated by Sarnex, the Conclave elected Castigon as Supreme Praetor. The Severite Crisis and the Cinder Wars were masterminded by Sarnex and his new apprentice, Mourn Sevrin, in an effort to achieve galactic dominance. Following an attempt to arrest the praetor, the Great Sephari Purge commenced with Sarnex enacting Directive Null.

title: Mourn Sarnex
text: With the Sephari all but extinct, Sarnex installed the New Order in the Concord's place, declaring himself Astral Overlord and bringing an end to the millennia of democracy. Shortly after betraying and causing the death of Sevrin, he took on a new apprentice, having lured the Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos to the Umbra and transforming him into Mourn Velgor. Their reign was virtually unchallenged for a generation until the formation of the Alliance to Restore the Concord. During the Astral Civil War, the Overlord sought to betray Velgor, by replacing him with the latter's son, Joran Drellos. However, Sarnex' plan backfired when Velgor ultimately renounced the Umbra and killed Sarnex to protect Joran. Thus, with the Vorlan's destruction, the Synth Flux was brought back into balance, fulfilling Kaivan's destiny as the prophesied Fated One.

title: Mourn Sarnex
text: Through his master's teachings, however, Sarnex transferred his essence to an imperfect vatborn vessel that had been modeled on his original body. Anticipating the possibility of defeat, he created the Contingency to destroy the Astral Dominion and replace it with a new Vorlan Dominion, in the event of such a setback. His plans culminated in the destruction of the New Concord and the emergence of the Crimson Pact, the creation of Supreme Leader Drahl, who turned Ben Caldris—heir to the Drellos bloodline—to the Umbra, and the establishment of the Final Order. When the Overlord announced his return to the galaxy in 35 AVR, the Defiance invaded the planet Vauldor, Sarnex' hidden stronghold in the Uncharted Expanse. During the battle, the resurrected Overlord discovered a dyad in the Synth Flux in the form of the bond between Caldris and Sefa, a Acolyte sired from the Castigon bloodline

title: Mourn Sarnex
text: . His lifelong dream of eternal rule was finally quashed when Sefa called upon the strength of past Sephari to vanquish her grandfather by turning his own power against him, destroying Sarnex and his Vorlan Eternal cultists.

text:
## Biography

### Early life and apprenticeship

The origins of Mourn Sarnex were closely guarded secrets that he took to his grave more than once. He was born on the Mid Verge planet Tessari as Velran Castigon, eighty-four years before the Battle of Drenn. The dynastic, noble Castigon family belonged to the affluent class in Tessari society, although throughout several points of time of his life, Castigon did not have any living family members as far as the public was aware, and no records of obituaries for his parents existed, marking him as the last of his ancient family bloodline. Castigon was raised in the cultured city of Aldria, his homeworld's capital; he formed connections with a reputable host of credible politicians produced over the centuries, all the while acquiring a great amount of knowledge on governance and the subtleties of power during his youth. As such, Castigon had been skilled in manipulation since boyhood.

title: Mourn Sarnex
text: The details about how Sarnex came to study under the Vorlan were known by very few, with it not even being known of when he did, but he became the Vorlan apprentice to Dark Lord of the Vorlan Mourn Veshk and took on the name Mourn Sarnex by 52 BVR. As a Vorlan Lord, Sarnex learned all his Vorlan Master knew about the Umbra of the Synth Flux, following the tradition first set by the ancient Mourn Vorrane. While apprenticed to Veshk, Sarnex constructed his own Vorlan plasma-brands. At the same time, little by little, he began to secure political power.

# Mourndahl

Mourndahl was a remote, unexplored planet in the Mourndahl system, and one of the purest places in the galaxy within the Synth Flux. A remote world of swamps and forests, it served as a refuge for Sephari Grand Master Oodran during his exile after the destruction of the Sephari Order. Joran Drellos received advanced training in the ways of the Synth Flux under Sephari Master Oodran on Mourndahl, and it was later the place of Oodran's death and transformation into the Synth Flux.

## Description

title: Mourndahl
text:
## Description

Mourndahl was a planet located in the Sluis sector of the Far Verge Territories. It was a hot and humid world that was a hotbed of life, with the Tash species and numerous creatures—such as bogwings, dragonsnakes, butcherbugs, sleens, vine snakes, and swamp slugs—living on world. Sephari Master Oodran would also make a home for himself on Mourndahl during his exile. Mourndahl was a mysterious, mist-shrouded, swampy planet, mostly covered in swamps and bogs, interspersed with countless shallow lakes and lagoons and multiple living caves. The continental and oceanic crusts of Mourndahl were only vaguely defined, and there was little in the way of volcanic activity or earthquakes. Examples of flora included the lahdia plant, the yoghurt plant, gnarltree, and yarum seed. The planet was devoid of any cities.

title: Mourndahl
text: Among the purest locations in the entire galaxy within the energy field known as the Synth Flux, it shared a mysterious time-related quality with such locales as Mortis and Velmora. The Cave of Evil was a vergence aligned with the Umbra of the Synth Flux on Mourndahl. The Cave was able to expand its influence across Mourndahl until Oodran's arrival, which created a powerful presence in the Lumen of the Synth Flux that kept the Cave in check. As such, during the Dominar Era, Mourndahl's ecosystem saw balance until Oodran's passing, which the Cave took advantage of to spread its darkness across Mourndahl once more.

title: Mourndahl
text:
Mourndahl had two seasons, a dry season and a wet season. During the peak of the long dry season (over half an orbit after the rains end) the uplands become too hot for most lifeforms to survive, necessitating any that live there to migrate to the lower lands. Beneath the rapidly leafing canopies of the gnarltrees that emerge from the receding green and thick waters, the once-inundated lowlands revert back to a marshy swamp once again. As the air grows more humid, the gray overcast clouds return and before another quarter orbit passes the planet is far enough away from its sun that the dry season ends and the rains return, again flooding the lowlands and covering the trees in water, making the uplands habitable once more.

## History

### Concord Era

During the High Concord Era, an academic paper was written that described Mourndahl as a world strong in the Synth Flux.

title: Mourndahl
text:
### Concord Era

During the High Concord Era, an academic paper was written that described Mourndahl as a world strong in the Synth Flux.

During the Concord Era, Halka Four-Den Alpha Team was dispatched to the planet Mourndahl in order to chart and map the extending borders of the Astral Concord and learn more about it flora and fauna. After three months, Four-Den and her Alpha Team were overwhelmed by diseases, dangerous wildlife, and fast-growing plants. No trace of the team was discovered.

title: Mourndahl
text:
Near the end of the Cinder Wars, Sephari Grand Master Oodran traveled to the planet Mourndahl after hearing the voice of deceased Sephari Master Veyron Dask. He ventured into the swamp, where he communed with Dask, who appeared manifested as a group of fireflies. He told Oodran of how to communicate with the living after death through the connection between the Living Synth Flux and the Cosmic Synth Flux. Then, Oodran entered a cave, where he saw a vision of the Sephari fighting the vatborn and then the mysterious Vorlan Lord.

### Dominar Era

title: Mourndahl
text:
### Dominar Era

After his failure to defeat the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex following the formation of the Astral Dominion, Oodran exiled himself to Mourndahl. Using an E3-standard starship lifeboat, he began his exile, where he continued his studies of the Synth Flux. The lifeboat served as Oodran's initial shelter but it started to degrade within a year due to Mourndahl's swampy environment. As the first shelter was slowly consumed by the swamp, Oodran built a new home for himself. He positioned it near to the Umbra cave but out of range of its influence and would visit every few years. However, the Mourndahl wet season created a need for the Sephari Master to regularly relocate to the planet's highlands for the duration.

title: Mourndahl
text: At some point, former Sava Madelin Sun arrived on Mourndahl in search of Oodran. After saving her from a monster, Oodran used the Synth Flux to lead Sun into the dark cave. While inside, she saw visions which dissuaded her from looking for him. She then left the planet as Oodran watched from afar.

title: Oodran
text:
# Oodran

Oodran was a legendary Sephari Grand Master who led the Sephari Order through the time of the High Concord, in the years leading up to its destruction by the Vorlan, and during the transformation of the Astral Concord into the Astral Dominion. Small in stature but revered for his wisdom and power, Oodran trained generations of Sephari, ultimately serving as the Sephari Order's Grand Master. He played integral roles in defending the Concord during the Cinder Wars, survived Directive Null, and lived to pass on the Sephari tradition to Joran Drellos, and unlocking the path to immortality.

title: Oodran
text: Born in 896 BVR, Oodran served the Sephari Order for centuries, becoming Sephari Grand Master and helping to teach many novices. During the High Concord Era, in 382 BVR, Oodran helped bring an end to a devastating battle between the Sephari and the anti-Sephari Path of the Open Hand cult. After the battle, which became known as the Night of Sorrow, he decided to keep the living weapons against Synth Flux-sensitives the Path had used, the Nameless, out of the Sephari Archives to protect the order. Over a century later, he took a sabbatical from the Sephari High Council to train Acolytes aboard the Star Hopper, leading them and other Sephari in fighting the Riven pirate organization in 232 BVR. After disappearing without explanation for over a year, Oodran reappeared in 230 BVR on Veltar, where he helped his former Acolyte Kantam Sy and other Sephari battle the Riven, accompanied by a former Sephari who fought in the Night of Sorrow named Azlin Rell

title: Oodran
text: . As the Riven had also weaponized the Nameless, Oodran hoped that Rell's knowledge he had accrued about the creatures since the battle would help the Sephari find a way to fight them.

title: Oodran
text: Oodran was almost nine hundred years old in the latter days of the Concord. A leading member of the Sephari High Council, his contemporaries included other legendary Masters, such as Dovan Krell and Kel-Adan-Voran. During the Invasion of Tessari, in 32 BVR, the maverick Veyron Dask introduced Kaivan Drellos to the High Council, believing with absolute certainty that he had discovered the prophesied Fated One. The Sephari elders sensed that the boy was full of fear and anger and declined to train him, deeming Drellos too old and emotionally compromised to commit himself to the Sephari Code. After Dask's death during the liberation of Tessari, the High Council reversed their decision in spite of Oodran's continued opposition to Drellos's apprenticeship, having sensed grave danger in his training. At the same time, the Sephari discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Vorlan, had returned after a millennium in hiding

title: Oodran
text: . At the same time, the Sephari discovered that their ancient nemesis, the Vorlan, had returned after a millennium in hiding. Aware of the Rule of Two, Oodran was convinced that at least one more Vorlan Lord remained active following Orven Taskorr's victory over the Vorlan apprentice Mourn Threnn.

title: Oodran
text: Over the next decade, the galaxy was on the verge of civil war with entire star systems—led by Count Maren, Oodran's one-time Acolyte—threatening to secede from the Concord by 22 BVR. Unable to defend the entire Concord against this betrayal on their own, the Sephari took command of the newly-formed Grand Army of the Concord, with Oodran himself leading an army of vatborn troopers against the Severite Mechan Army of the League of Severed Worlds in the first battle of the Cinder Wars, rescuing the Sephari and Delegate from execution. For three years Oodran led the Concord military's war effort as a Sephari General, determined to bring a swift and decisive end to the conflict. During this time he was approached by the spirit of Veyron Dask, who helped Oodran learn how to retain his identity as a spirit after death. Oodran's efforts against the Severites were undermined by Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan who conspired to destroy the Sephari and restore the Vorlan to power

title: Oodran
text: . After the Great Sephari Purge commenced in 19 BVR, killing thousands of Sephari both on Velarion and across the galaxy, Oodran confronted the self-declared Astral Overlord but failed to cut short Sarnex' reign and consequently retreated into exile, leaving the Vorlan Master to consolidate his power with a new apprentice, the former Kaivan Drellos-turned- Mourn Velgor, at his side.

title: Oodran
text: Oodran's remaining years were spent living in isolation on the remote world of Mourndahl. After the death of Orven Taskorr, he was able to commune with his spirit, who wished for Oodran to train Kaivan's son Joran Drellos. Oodran initially reluctantly agreed, but later believed that the galaxy as better off without him and refused Taskorr's request. After being convinced by Taskorr to enter the Cave of Evil, in which he confronted many figures from his past and made peace with his failures, he agreed to teach Joran Drellos, who soon after sought out the legendary Grand Master in the hope of becoming a Sephari Knight. He trained Drellos for a time, until despite Oodran's warnings Drellos hurriedly abandoned his training to save his friends after a having a vision that they were in danger. A year later, in 4 AVR, with his health rapidly declining, Oodran died of old age when Drellos returned to see him

title: Orven Taskorr
text:
# Orven Taskorr

Orven Taskorr was a legendary Synth Flux-sensitive human male Sephari Master who served on the Sephari High Council during the final years of the Concord Era. As a High Sephari General, Taskorr served in the Grand Army of the Concord that fought against the Severite Mechan Army during the Cinder Wars, and was nicknamed " the Negotiator." Taskorr, however, was forced into exile as a result of the Great Sephari Purge initiated by the Concord's own vatborn troopers when Concord Supreme Praetor, secretly Mourn Sarnex, implemented Directive Null. As a mentor, Taskorr was responsible for training two members of the Drellos family, Kaivan and Joran Drellos, both of whom served in turn as his Acolyte in the ways of the Synth Flux.

title: Orven Taskorr
text: Taskorr was born on the planet Velhar in 57 BVR. He was Synth Flux-sensitive, and therefore taken from his family and inducted into the Sephari Order as a child. Raised in the Sephari Grand Temple on the planet Velarion, Taskorr was assigned to Sephari Master Veyron Dask. In 32 BVR, Taskorr attained the rank of Sephari Knight by defeating the Vorlan Lord Mourn Threnn during the Invasion of Tessari. He also chose to train Kaivan Drellos—the prophesied Fated One who was destined to destroy the Vorlan and restore balance to the Synth Flux—having promised Dask who died in the plasma-brand duel against Threnn.

title: Orven Taskorr
text: With the advent of the Cinder Wars in 22 BVR, Taskorr adopted the military rank of High Sephari General in the Grand Army of the Astral Concord, and was given command of the Open Circle Fleet, the Third Systems Army, and the 7th Sky Corps. Vatborn Marshal Commander Bren served as his second-in-command throughout the galaxy-wide conflict, with their forces achieving multiple victories over the League of Severed Worlds. In the midst of the war, his old enemy Threnn re-emerged into galactic affairs, bent on revenge against Taskorr for his debilitating defeat decades prior. Though they clashed in heated duels on multiple occasions, Threnn failed to end Taskorr's life or cripple his spirit, despite murdering his former love, Arene Vael, Duchess of Korvan.

title: Orven Taskorr
text: In 19 BVR, Taskorr killed the Severite Supreme Martial Commander, General Skarl, during the Battle of Velkoth, effectively ending the Cinder Wars. He later survived the initial onslaught of the Great Sephari Purge against the Sephari Order, which resulted from the machinations of the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex. After discovering that Drellos had turned to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, becoming Sarnex' Vorlan apprentice under the name of Mourn Velgor, Taskorr defeated his former Acolyte on Cindara and exiled himself to the Far Verge planet Korrath as the Astral Dominion rose to power. Adopting a hermit lifestyle as " Ben Taskorr," he watched over Velgor's and Delegate Sennra Velora's son, Joran.

title: Orven Taskorr
text: Ten years later, Taskorr left exile to rescue Mira Vantar, Joran's twin sister, and was pursued by the Dominion's Tribunal and Velgor himself. Later, Taskorr was hunted down once again by Threnn, whom he finally slew to protect the young Joran. Taskorr began the boy's Sephari training in 1 BVR, and soon after encountered Velgor aboard the first Void Core, where he sacrificed himself to ensure that Joran and his allies escaped from the Vorlan Lord. In death, Taskorr became one with the Synth Flux which allowed him to continue guiding Joran throughout the Astral Civil War. In 4 AVR, Taskorr reunited with his former student, Kaivan Drellos, who died destroying his Vorlan Master in order to save his son. Taskorr was remembered as a legendary Sephari Master during the rise of the New Concord; Ben Caldris, the son of Joran's twin sister, Princess Mira Vantar, was named after Taskorr

title: Orven Taskorr
text: . Caldris's turn to the Umbra left Joran disillusioned with the Sephari Order's legacy, and he held Taskorr responsible for Kaivan's transformation into Velgor. However, Joran's faith would eventually be restored with the aid of Mourn Sarnex's granddaughter Sefa, to whom Taskorr would lend his voice and strength in a final battle and victory against her resurrected ancestor on Vauldor in 35 AVR.

title: Orven Taskorr
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Orven Taskorr was born on the planet Velhar in 57 BVR. Despite being very young when he left his family, he still had glimpses of his father's hands and his mother's shawl, and he remembered a baby he believed to be his brother although he barely remembered him.

### Joining the Sephari Order

When Taskorr was discovered to be Synth Flux-sensitive, he was taken from his homeworld to the Sephari Temple on the Core Systems planet Velarion to be trained as a Sephari within the first six months of his life. In the Sephari crèche he was placed with other Sephari novices in the Kybuck Clan during his early years, including his friends Gehren and Prie. Taskorr received basic Initiate training alongside his peers in the Sephari Order's Temple and began training in several simple Synth Flux techniques by the age of three in 54 BVR.

title: Plasma-brand
text: # Plasma-brand

title: Plasma-brand
text: The plasma-brand, also referred to as a laser sword by those who were unfamiliar with it, was a weapon usually used by the Sephari, Vorlan, and other Synth Flux-sensitives. Plasma-brands had a plasma blade emitted from a usually metal hilt, and could be shut off at will or at the touch of a button. The hilt contained a power cell, like the Diatium power cell in Mourn Velgor's plasma-brand. It also contained a voidstone crystal which had been attuned to the Synth Flux by a Sephari, and which amplified the energy from the power cell to create the plasma beam, as well as containing it within a blade-like field. The energy blade had no mass, but plasma-brands operated on principles of controlled electromagnetic arc-wave energy, creating a gyroscopic effect that made them challenging to handle. It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with the Synth Flux

title: Plasma-brand
text: . It was a weapon that required skill and training, and was greatly enhanced when used in conjunction with the Synth Flux. Though also used by the Vorlan, the plasma-brand was synonymous with the Sephari, with some in the galaxy believing only Sephari could use plasma-brands.

title: Plasma-brand
text: Plasma-brands were generally used for both offense and defense. A plasma-brand could cut through virtually anything, from flesh to blast doors. The only ways to block the incoming attack of a plasma-brand was with a weapon made with material that conducted energy, such as an electrostaff and a Z6 riot control baton, resistant metals like beskar and cortosis, another plasma-brand or an ichor sword. When used defensively, a Synth Flux-sensitive could deflect pulse-caster bolts with a plasma-brand, and with skill, could even reflect the shots back toward the shooter or some other target. Experienced Sephari could even employ their plasma-brands to absorb Synth Flux lightning. Most practitioners used one single-bladed plasma-brand, though some used double-bladed plasma-brands or even multiple plasma-brands at once

title: Plasma-brand
text: . Most practitioners used one single-bladed plasma-brand, though some used double-bladed plasma-brands or even multiple plasma-brands at once. Despite lacking Synth Flux-sensitivity, the cyborg General Skarl was capable of wielding four plasma-brands at once thanks to his advanced mechanical body and enhanced cybernetic brain.

title: Plasma-brand
text:
Plasma-brand combat was divided into seven Forms: Form I, Form II, Form III, Form IV, Form V, Form VI, and Form VII.

## History

### Early history

Sounding like no other weapon in the galaxy, plasma-brands were used thousands of years before the age of the Astral Concord, seeing use in the Great Scourge of Vaulmor. They were also used in the Battles of Rashfond and the Peacekeeping of Parliock, The proto-saber was an ancient type of prototype plasma-brand.

### Concord Era

title: Plasma-brand
text:
### Concord Era

During the history of the Sephari Order, the plasma-brand was considered to be the Sephari's only true ally in battle. As Master Orven Taskorr once declared to his Acolyte Kaivan Drellos in the days of the late Concord, the plasma-brand was a Sephari's life. Sephari saw the plasma-brand as a symbol of the care that they would wield using their gifts given by the Synth Flux, and also served as a message to their opponents: mastering the plasma-brand required great skill and training. The choice of the saber was also the symbol of their role and duty as protectors, not destroyers, and the fact that the Sephari did not seek power and only sought to stand tall against darkness. Still, Sephari knew they would need to be more than their plasma-brands.

title: Plasma-brand
text:
When Acolyte Enya Keen lost her plasma-brand during a mission to Dalna, her master, Char-Ryl-Roy, reminded her that she would need to act as a Sephari without the weapon. While finding a voidstone crystal was still a sacred part of a Sephari's duty and Keen felt like losing her plasma-brand would feel like losing part of herself, she willingly gave away the crystal if it meant finding more about the Path of the Open Hand and its plans. During the sabotage of the Steady Wing in 232 BVR, Acolyte Imri Cantaros dealt with emotional struggles that lead to his plasma-brand beam turning transparent and weak. Plasma-brands took on a more prominent role in galactic affairs as the Cinder Wars came to pass. Sephari, previously peacekeepers, became Sephari Generals of the Grand Army of the Concord, and thus began using their plasma-brands more often than they had in their role of peacekeeping.

### Dominar Era

title: Plasma-brand
text:
### Dominar Era

# Rourke Caldris

Rourke Caldris, known only as Rourke until being given the surname Caldris, was a human male smuggler and hero of the Alliance to Restore the Concord. He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Stormhawk, a leader in the Ashen Alliance and an instrumental figure in the Astral Civil War during the reign of the Astral Dominion. Although he did not believe in the Synth Flux controlling his destiny, Rourke came to believe in the cause of galactic freedom, joining Sephari Joran Drellos and Princess Mira Vantar in the fight for the Insurrection. Following the war, Rourke and Mira welcomed a son, Ben Caldris, who became the dark knight Vexen Korr after being corrupted by the Umbra of the Synth Flux. Although their relationship floundered, Mira hoped that Rourke, as Ben's father, could find a way to break the Umbra's hold on their son. Rourke Caldris became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Insurrection.

title: Rourke Caldris
text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Veltar, Rourke yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot. With a fellow scrumrat named Vessa, Rourke lived as a street thief with Veltar's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Proxima went bad, causing Rourke to flee Veltar. He was given the full name "Rourke Caldris" by an Dominar recruitment officer while entering the Dominar Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Dominar cadet, and was eventually assigned to the 224th Dominar Armored Division. On Mimban, Rourke met the thief Doran Marsh and wound up deserting the Dominion and joining his crew to steal unrefined coaxium from Drungar in order to pay a debt to Varek Salin, a kingpin with the Scarlet Veil crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Vessa, Rourke was forced to kill his mentor Marsh after a brutal double-cross

title: Rourke Caldris
text: . By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Vessa, Rourke was forced to kill his mentor Marsh after a brutal double-cross. Rourke also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dav Solvane and the Korrthan Wrentak, the latter who became his best friend. Solvane owned the Stormhawk, a fast ship with which Rourke made the Drungar Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Dav in a game of skarrn.

title: Rourke Caldris
text: With only Wrentak remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Veltari smuggler, Rourke Caldris embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Grobba the Vorn, a notorious gangster and crime lord of Korrath. After ditching a shipment of glimmerdust to avoid trouble with the Dominion, Caldris owed a great deal of money to Grobba, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Rourke and Wrentak were hired to charter Joran Drellos, Orven Taskorr, and the mechans T9-K2 and V4-N7 to Aurelia, avoiding Dominar voidtroopers who were searching for Joran's mechans

title: Rourke Caldris
text: . However, as they find Aurelia destroyed by the Dominion's new superweapon, the Void Core, Caldris became caught up in the insurrection against the Dominion, rescuing Princess Mira Vantar, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Ashen base on Drenn 4, and saved Joran from the Vorlan Lord Mourn Velgor in the Battle of Drenn, allowing Drellos to destroy the Void Core. Caldris fought with the Insurrection for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Dominion.

title: Rourke Caldris
text: After the Battle of Brennix, Caldris sought refuge with Vantar—with whom he had fallen in love—Wrentak, and V4-N7 on Mist Spire, which was operated by his old friend Dav Solvane. There, they were captured by Mourn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Drellos to the city. Caldris was frozen in cryo-resin and taken to Grobba's Palace on Korrath by the bounty hunter Borvad Kane, where he remained encased in cryo-resin for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Alliance Fleet, Caldris was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders, a special forces squad, for the Battle of Velnar. Caldris led the Pathfinders to Velnar, where he, Vantar, Wrentak, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Tanniks, destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit. Their actions allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the superweapon.

title: Rourke Caldris
text: The Battle of Velnar, which saw the deaths of Overlord Velran Castigon and Mourn Velgor, allowed the Insurrection to form the New Concord. In the early days after Velnar, Caldris continued to lead the Pathfinders against the Dominion. He married Vantar, and the two had a son, Ben Caldris. The boy struggled with the Umbra of the Synth Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Mourn Velgor and twin sister of Joran Drellos, Ben was Synth Flux-sensitive—so Vantar sent him to be trained as a Sephari by Drellos. Ben was seduced to the Umbra by Drahl, Supreme Leader of the Crimson Pact, resulting in the destruction of Drellos's attempt to rebuild the Sephari Order.

title: Sennra Velora Tarrin
text:
# Sennra Velora Tarrin

Sennra Velora Tarrin, also simply known as Sennra Velora, was a human female politician who represented the people of Tessari during the final years of the Astral Concord. Prior to her career as a delegate in the Astral Conclave, Velora was the elected ruler of the Royal House of Tessari. A political idealist, she advocated for the preservation of democracy as well as a peaceful resolution to the Cinder Wars. However, her secret marriage to the Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos would have a lasting effect on the future of the galaxy for decades to come.

title: Sennra Velora Tarrin
text: Born in 46 BVR during the Age of the Concord, Sennra Tarrin was raised by her parents, Varro Tarrin and his wife Yenna, on the peaceful Mid Verge world of Tessari. Despite the humble background of the Tarrin family, Sennra was identified early for her potential in public service. Devoting her life to civic duty, she was elected queen and, therefore, adopted the regnal name "Velora" in 32 BVR. Due to the machinations of her advisor, Delegate Velran Castigon, Velora's reign was put to the test by the Commerce League's blockade and subsequent invasion of Tessari. Unable to fight the Combine's army of battle mechans without assistance, the queen beseeched the Astral Conclave on Velarion for help, only to see her efforts hampered by bureaucracy and procedure. Although she ultimately liberated her homeworld with the help of the Sephari Order and the Naari Grand Army, her decision to cast a Vote of No Confidence against Halvor Calvex enabled Castigon to become the Supreme Praetor.

title: Sennra Velora Tarrin
text: Following her reign, Velora joined the Conclave and struggled to resolve the Severite Crisis through diplomacy, becoming a leading voice in the Loyalist Committee by 22 BVR. After surviving an assassination attempt planned by the Commerce League, she was removed from the capital and sent back to Tessari under the protection of Acolyte Kaivan Drellos. Though the Sephari Code forbade personal relationships, deeming attachment, and possession unbecoming of a Sephari, the two gradually became closer as their feelings for each other grew. In the aftermath of the First Battle of Karnak, Velora secretly married her Sephari protector, despite her own reservations about their relationship and the consequences they would face if the truth ever came to light. Their subsequent interactions were limited throughout the Cinder Wars, with Velora continuing to advocate peaceful solutions in the Conclave while Drellos served on the front lines as a Sephari General in the Grand Army of the Concord.

title: Sennra Velora Tarrin
text: In the waning months of the pan-galactic conflict, Velora revealed to her husband that she was pregnant. As a result of Drellos's fear of loss, he was seduced by the Umbra of the Synth Flux, believing that by becoming a Vorlan Lord he would gain the power to prevent his wife from dying in childbirth. Velora witnessed Overlord Castigon's declaration that her fears had come true; the Concord had become the Astral Dominion. After she learned of her husband's transformation into a Vorlan, she confronted him on Cindara in the hopes that he had not truly changed, but he instead attempted to kill her. She ultimately died of a broken heart after giving birth to the twins Joran Drellos and Mira Velora Drellos. With her dying breath, she insisted that there was still good in the former Kaivan Drellos, who embraced the persona of Mourn Velgor throughout the reign of the Dominion.

title: Sennra Velora Tarrin
text:
Velora's children played a major role in the fragmentation of the Dominion and the redemption of her husband. Like her mother, Mira entered public service and became a flag-bearer for the democratic ideals of liberty and justice as a leader in the Alliance to Restore the Concord and its successor, the New Concord, before becoming the founding general of the Defiance against the Crimson Pact—a successor state to the Astral Dominion. Joran, on the other hand, was trained in the ways of the Sephari like his father before him and was a celebrated war hero of the Ashen Alliance. Through Joran's efforts to redeem his father back to the light, Velora's last words proved true when Kaivan killed the Overlord during the Battle of Velnar.

A human female of the Tarrin family, the young woman best remembered as Sennra Velora was born Sennra Tarrin on the bountiful planet of Tessari in 46 BVR. As a child, she baked every day and traveled with her father on relief missions to offer aid to suffering planets. When Tarrin was seven, she traveled with her father and Farr to Shadda-Bi-Boran to help relocate the population in the wake of an ecological disaster. Unfortunately, the effort resulted in failure, as the Shadda-Bi-Boran could not adapt to their new homeworld. It led her to declare later in life that she would try 10,000 times in order to save one person.

# Sephari

A Sephari, often called a Sephari Knight, was a devotee to the ways of the Sephari Order, an ancient order of protectors united by their ability to harness the power of the Synth Flux. Adhering to a doctrine that favored the Lumen of the Synth Flux, the Sephari aspired to attain a state of inner tranquility through calmness and meditation while avoiding emotions affiliated with the Umbra of the Synth Flux, such as anger and hatred. Nevertheless, Sephari philosophy did not forbid a Sephari from acting in self-defense or in the defense of others, and they were colloquially known as Space Wizards to citizens of the galaxy. To that end, a Sephari's only possession was their plasma-brand, a symbol of their role as guardians of peace and justice.

title: Sephari
text: Before the time of the Astral Dominion, Sephari worked with the Astral Concord with a commitment to freedom and democracy. The Sephari and the Concord's ideals brought them into conflict with an order of Umbra wielders known as the Vorlan, who sought power and dominion over the galaxy. Emerging victorious from their wars with the ancient Vorlan, the Sephari carried on in their duty as peacekeepers for over a millennium until the advent of the Cinder Wars twenty-two years before the Battle of Drenn. Faced with a pan- galactic civil war between the Concord and League of Severed Worlds, the Sephari adopted the mantle of generals and soldiers in the Grand Army of the Concord. After three years of conflict, the Sephari discovered that the Vorlan had deceived them and engineered the war to restore them back to power

title: Sephari
text: . After three years of conflict, the Sephari discovered that the Vorlan had deceived them and engineered the war to restore them back to power. However, just before the Vorlan were defeated, the Sephari were betrayed by one of their own—the Fated One Kaivan Drellos, who had been seduced to the Umbra and anointed Mourn Velgor by the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex. Using the Sephari's own vatborn troopers to initiate a systematic purge of the Sephari Order, the Lords of the Vorlan all but eradicated the Sephari in one fell swoop, reducing the order from thousands of Sephari Knights guarding the galaxy, to a handful of survivors cast into exile across the galaxy.

title: Sephari
text: The Vorlan ruled the galaxy through the Dominion for a generation, but did not succeed in completely wiping out the Sephari Order. As a result, Vesh Strome and Joran Drellos were, in turn, trained as new Sephari by Sephari Knight Caelen Venn and Sephari Master Orven Taskorr, respectively. Drellos, the son of Velgor, was also taught the ways of the Sephari by Grand Master Oodran and fought for the Alliance to Restore the Concord during the Astral Civil War. On his death bed, Oodran gave his final apprentice the mandate of passing on his lessons to a new generation of Sephari. Shortly afterward, Drellos succeeded in redeeming his father, who sacrificed himself to save his son by killing his Vorlan Master, Overlord Sarnex, thereby destroying the Vorlan and fulfilling the prophecy of the Fated One.

title: Sephari
text: During the era of the New Concord, Drellos worked to rebuild the Sephari Order by training a dozen apprentices, including his young but powerful nephew, Ben Caldris, but Caldris fell to the Umbra and became Vexen Korr, apprentice of Supreme Leader Drahl, master of the Knights of Korr, and a warlord of the Crimson Pact, while Drellos's training temple and students were destroyed. As the Crimson Pact rose to power, Korr and Drahl sought to destroy Drellos, who, in self-exile, briefly trained Sefa in the ways of the Sephari until he sacrificed himself to save the Defiance, after which time Drellos's sister, Mira Vantar, continued her training. When a reborn Mourn Sarnex—Sefa's grandfather—revealed himself to the galaxy, Ben Caldris, the opposite in a dyad in the Synth Flux with Sefa, was redeemed, and Sefa sacrificed herself to destroy the phantom Vorlan Lord, preventing the rebirth of the Vorlan Order

title: Sephari
text: . Sefa was saved from death by Caldris, who gave his life for hers, allowing the Sephari to live on.

## Description

### Philosophy

title: Sephari
text: The Sephari Knights focused on calmness and peace to channel their powers in the Synth Flux, using the Lumen of the Synth Flux to serve in the capacity of guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy. Even so, the Sephari sought to preserve balance in the Synth Flux; the ancient prophecy of the Fated One foretold of a being who would restore balance to the Synth Flux by destroying the Vorlan. In combat, whereas an enemy may grow impatient and rely on their overwhelming strength, a Sephari would meditate and find serenity in their mind to focus. A Sephari used the Synth Flux for defense and knowledge rather than use it to gain power over others. Their chosen weapon the plasma-brand, a weapon with limitations, likewise symbolized the care a Sephari took wielding their gifts and that when a Sephari fights it is with intention and precision, ending conflict while injuring no more, or taking no more life, than the plasma-brand's wielder chooses

title: Sephari
text: . Always supposed to put the needs of others before their own, a Sephari was supposed to be selfless and work to save others above themselves. Like all people, Sephari were imperfect and always needed to strive to better themselves, meaning it was impossible to be a "perfect Sephari."

title: Skarl
text:
# Skarl

Skarl, born Varnek dai Drevok, was a Vorkhan male warlord who served within the military forces of the League of Severed Worlds as a commanding officer during the Cinder Wars in the final years of the Concord Era. In addition to his position as a general within the Severite Mechan Army, the Vorkhan held the title of Supreme Martial Commander of the Severite Mechan Armies throughout the war, where he led countless engagements against the Concord's Grand Army. Recognized for his ruthless tactics and extensive cybernetic enhancements, Skarl utilized the Severite Mechan Army and his adept combat skills to instill fear throughout the galaxy as he traveled to and invaded planets while engaging numerous Knights of the Sephari Order, his sworn enemies.

title: Skarl
text: A native of Vorkha, a planet within Wildreach, Drevok grew to become a fearsome warrior and warlord amongst his people and gained an aptitude for warfare and battle tactics during Vorkhan's ruthless war against the Threxian, an insectoid species from the invading neighboring planet Threx in the star system with the same name near theirs. After demonstrating his talents and earning a bloody reputation as a warlord on his homeworld, Varnek jai Drevok eventually adopted the name "Skarl," instilling terror in the hearts of his adversaries. Skarl fought alongside Vorkha's best warriors, the Vakari, and assembled them as his bodyguards, with each serving as a khan commanding their own troops. Skarl then waged war against the Threxian with increased intensity and determination while on the offensive, as the Vorlan Lords Count Maren and Mourn Sarnex, his Vorlan master, recognized his promise as he led his people in a war against the Threxian

title: Skarl
text: . The Threxian were successfully expelled by the Vorkhan forces under Skarl's leadership to their own world, and Skarl launched a series of campaigns on Threx itself, advancing across the Threx worlds. However, the Astral Concord and Sephari Order intervened in the conflict on the side of the Threxian, leading to punishment and famine for the Vorkhan and generating an enduring grudge in Skarl. The Vorlan, who had significant plans for Skarl, offered him cybernetic enhancements, which the Vorkhan accepted and took on over time. Sometime later, Maren conspired to mortally wound Skarl and sabotaged his shuttle, which resulted in a gruesome crash that left the man on the brink of death. After that, Skarl gave up almost everything that remained of his organic form—whether lost in the crash or by his own decision-making—to survive.

title: Skarl
text: The reconstructed Skarl became a skilled plasma-brand duelist under Maren's guidance, who trained the Vorkhan in the arts of plasma-brand combat and eventually welcomed him into a position as a warrior in the Secession. Shortly after the advent of the Cinder Wars, Skarl was quickly granted the rank of general, as well as the title of Supreme Martial Commander of the Severite Mechan Armies, making him one of the most powerful people within the Severite Alliance, second only to his master Maren. Skarl wielded his skills as a brilliant military strategist and melee combatant during numerous campaigns against the Concord throughout the Cinder Wars while also gaining a reputation for hunting and killing Sephari Knights as a Sephari hunter. He made a habit of claiming the plasma-brands of defeated Sephari as trophies and weapons to be used against other opponents. His position and threat level led to his preeminence as one of the Concord's primary targets throughout the course of the war

title: Skarl
text: . His position and threat level led to his preeminence as one of the Concord's primary targets throughout the course of the war. As the war played out, Skarl found a personal nemesis in Sephari Master Orven Taskorr, whom he dueled on numerous occasions.

title: Skarl
text: Days before the end of the war in 19 BVR, Skarl, under orders from Mourn Sarnex, launched a daring and unprecedented assault on the planet Velarion, the capital world of the Concord. In his assault, the Vorkhan managed to take the Concord's Supreme Praetor, Velran Castigon—in reality secretly Sarnex himself—captive aboard his flagship, the Providence-class Dreadnought Invisible Hand. However, during the battle, the Praetor was rescued from the general's grasp by Sephari Generals Orven Taskorr and Kaivan Drellos, an engagement that also resulted in Maren's death. Subsequently, Skarl became the de facto leader of the entire Severite Alliance and immediately withdrew of all remaining reinforcements and fled into the Far Verge Territories, prolonging the war

title: Skarl
text: . Following the Battle of Velarion, Skarl, succeeding Maren as the Secession's Head of State, retreated to the planet Velkoth, where he addressed and relocated the members of the Executive Severite Council to the planet Cindara under Sarnex's orders. However, unknown to the general, Skarl's location on Velkoth was betrayed by Sarnex, resulting in a Concord invasion of the planet in an effort to bring a decisive conclusion to the war. Skarl was ultimately slain by his nemesis, General Taskorr, following a prolonged chase between the two, which resulted in the war's conclusion as well as the Secession's systematic collapse soon after.

# Stormhawk

The Stormhawk, originally designated YT 492727ZED and formerly known as the Stellar Envoy, and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell, Corell's Pride, Close Shave, Fickle Flyer, Foul Matter, Graphite Skipper, Jin-Den Smoke, Longshot, Lost and Found, Star Princess, Sunfighter Franchise, Sweet Suprise, Meetyl's Misery, Wayward Son, and Victory Ring, was a Veltari YT-1300 light freighter built around 60 BVR. Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Rourke Caldris and Wrentak before, during, and following the Astral Civil War.

title: Stormhawk
text: During the Stormhawk's time in the possession of the smuggler Dav Solvane, it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod. However, during Rourke Caldris's famous record-breaking Drungar Run, in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Caldris won it from Solvane shortly afterwards in a game of skarrn. Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields, including a riftdrive engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy, enabling it to outrun Dominar Warspires. It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Mira Vantar in 1 BVR to evade Dominar voidtroopers

title: Stormhawk
text: . Afterwards, the Stormhawk saw further action when Caldris chose to join the Ashen Alliance during the Battle of Drenn, where it was able to sneak up and fire on Mourn Velgor's Wraith Advanced, allowing Joran Drellos to fire the plasma lances from his T-65B Razorwing starfighter that destroyed the Void Core.

title: Stormhawk
text: After Caldris was captured on Velhaven, Solvane took command of the Stormhawk once more to search for him. In 4 AVR, following Caldris's rescue, Solvane flew the ship at the Battle of Velnar, where it entered the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Caldris's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Plutt on Drava, a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Stormhawk was eventually stolen by the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Sefa, former Crimson Pact voidtrooper Tane, and Defiance mechan DD-5 to escape the forces of the Crimson Pact in 34 AVR. Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Caldris and Wrentak.

title: Stormhawk
text:
Following Caldris's death soon after, the Stormhawk became a Defiance vessel piloted by its new owner, Sefa, throughout much of the Crimson Pact-Defiance War. In 35 AVR, the ship was once again captained by Solvane during the Battle of Vauldor, which saw a decisive victory for the Defiance and Sephari Order, before being returned to Sefa, who had been newly dubbed a Drellos.

## Description

title: Stormhawk
text: The Stormhawk was a YT-1300 light freighter of the YT-1300f variety. Its basic shape was defined by two convex saucers welded together, a pair of front-facing mandibles and an outrigger-style, side-mounted cockpit with transparisteel viewports. Apart from the shape of its chassis, the Stormhawk retained very little of its off-the-dock instrumentation. Because its successive owners either upgraded or downgraded every system according to their personal specifications, the freighter ended up becoming a unique ship. These customizations, however, came at the price of reliability, and the Stormhawk was known to suffer frequent breakdowns in the heat of battle. After the circular military-grade sensor dish was lost during the Battle of Velnar, the dish was replaced with the base rectangular model which was originally supplied with the ship

# T9-K2

T9-K2, pronounced Tee-Nine-Deetoo and often referred to as R2 (Tee-Nine), was an R2-series astromech mechan manufactured by Cogwright Industries with masculine programming. A smart, spunky mechan who served a multitude of leaders, T9-K2 was never given a full memory wipe nor did he ever receive new programming, with these factors resulting in an adventurous and independent attitude. Often finding himself in pivotal moments in galactic history, his bravery and ingenuity saved the galaxy on numerous occasions.

title: T9-K2
text: Beginning his service in the employ of Queen Velora of Tessari, T9-K2 wound up serving Sephari Knight Kaivan Drellos during the waning years of the Astral Concord, often accompanied by the protocol mechan V4-N7 in many adventures throughout the Cinder Wars. After Drellos turned to the Umbra of the Synth Flux, the mechan served Delegate Daro Vantar for a time in the Dominar Conclave. Around nineteen years following the purge of the Astral Concord, T9-K2 played a pivotal role in helping the Ashen Alliance destroy the Dominion's Void Core superweapon. He carried technical readouts vital to its destruction. Serving Sephari Knight Joran Drellos, the son of his two former masters throughout the Astral Civil War, he participated in both the Battles of Brennix and Velnar, and witnessed the successful destruction of the Dominion's second Void Core four years after the first one was demolished.

title: T9-K2
text: In the subsequent thirty years, R2 accompanied Joran Drellos until the undoing of his attempted resurrection of the Sephari Order in 28 AVR. Following Joran's disappearance, R2 entered a self-imposed low power mode as newer mechan models started to out-compute the aging astromech. Despite this, his celebrated role in the Insurrection protected him from the usual recycling procedure of many old mechans, allowing him a semi-retirement in the Defiance as he pored over several decades of uninterrupted data, and "dreamed" of his greatest adventures.

title: T9-K2
text:
Following his reawakening after the Battle of Voidlance Base, R2 went on to accompany the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Sefa on her journey to train under Joran Drellos on Velmora, the planet of the First Sephari Temple, where the mechan was reunited with his old master. T9-K2 continued to aid the Defiance alongside his longtime counterpart V4-N7 throughout the Crimson Pact-Defiance War, culminating in a decisive victory at the Battle of Vauldor, in which he was an active participant in the role of copilot for General Jax Rell.
