## Biography

### Serving Sennra Velora

T9-K2 was built around prior or during 32 BVR. He was one of several astromech mechans on Queen Sennra Velora's Tessari Royal Starship during the invasion of Tessari by the Commerce League that year. The ship was used by Queen Velora and her entourage in an attempt to pass the blockade and escape the planet. Unluckily for the passengers, the vessel took a hit to the shield generator from a Commerce League battleship. The four astromechs were sent out to repair the ship, but only T9-K2 survived—the rest were pulverized by stray pulse-caster fire. T9-K2 was able to bring the shields online by bypassing the main power drive, allowing the ship to narrowly escape into riftspace.

title: T9-K2
text: As the ship traveled to Korrath, T9-K2 was taken before Daxa, the Queen's decoy in the guise of Velora, where he was commended for his actions. The ship landed on Korrath without any further incidents, although the voyage fried the riftdrive. T9-K2 accompanied Sephari Master Veyron Dask, Naari exile Bimo Trask, and Sennra, the queen in disguise, to the city of Krevar Hollow to find a replacement. In the junk shop of the Brunni merchant Grezzo they found they could not afford a replacement riftdrive and later took shelter from a sandstorm in the home of Grezzo's slaves, a boy named Kaivan Drellos, and his mother, Mella.

title: T9-K2
text: At the Drellos home, T9-K2 met V4-N7, a protocol mechan that Kaivan had built. The two bonded as they worked on Kaivan's personal skiff-racer. T9-K2 and V4-N7 cheered for Kaivan during the Vorga Trials Classic, where the boy would win his freedom, along with enough money to buy a new riftdrive. T9-K2 accompanied the group to Velarion, and from there back to Tessari. As Queen Velora led an attempt to liberate the planet, T9-K2 nestled into an N-1 starfighter. Young Kaivan, being ordered to hide in the cockpit by Veyron Dask, accidentally launched the fighter and the two flew into battle, destroyed the Mechan Control Ship and shut down the mechan armies, winning the battle and liberating Tessari. T9-K2 and his allies later attended a victory parade in Aldria, though they were unable to be joined by Dask, as he had been killed by the Vorlan Lord Mourn Threnn during the battle

title: T9-K2
text: . Because of this, Drellos became the Acolyte learner to Orven Taskorr, who had been Dask's apprentice before the Sephari Master's death.

title: Tessari
text:
# Tessari

Tessari was a bountiful planet in the Chommell sector of the Mid Verge, in the Trailing Sectors and close to the border of the Far Verge Territories. It was home to the indigenous Naari species and to a population of humans known as the Tessari. Tessari was pushed to the forefront of galactic politics as the birthplace of the Dark Lord of the Vorlan Velran Castigon, who served as its representative in the Conclave of the Astral Concord.

title: Tessari
text: Under the guise of his Vorlan title Mourn Sarnex, Castigon secretly engineered an invasion of his peaceful homeworld by the Commerce League, a megacorporation in a bid for power. Ostensibly done in protest over proposed taxation of formerly free trade routes, the Combine's invasion led to an outpouring of support from the Conclave for both Castigon and the newly-elected Queen of Tessari, Sennra Velora. Velora led a successful resistance movement and removed the Combine from her world during the Battle of Tessari. Castigon subsequently rose to the office of the Supreme Praetor of the Concord, with Velora eventually taking his place as the planet's senatorial representative.

title: Tessari
text: Tessari would commit itself firmly to democracy in the intervening years, staying loyal to the Concord during the pan-galactic Cinder Wars, which saw several military engagements against the League of Severed Worlds come to the planet. By the time of the war's end, Castigon had amassed considerable power and proclaimed himself the head of a new Astral Dominion. Castigon's reign would eventually be ended by the Alliance to Restore the Concord, a ashen movement led by Velora's children, Mira Vantar and Joran Drellos.

title: Tessari
text:
Despite his origins on the planet, Castigon did not care at all for his homeworld and, following his death, Tessari was named a priority target for Operation: Cinder, a protocol that the Vorlan Lord had put in place to destroy Dominar worlds should they fail to protect their Overlord. Through the intervention of Vantar and Queen Sosha Soruna, however, Tessari was spared from ruin and went on to become a member of the successor state to the Alliance, the New Concord. Decades later, the planet would again fight against tyranny, rising up against the military junta of the Crimson Pact during its war with Vantar's Defiance.

## Description

title: Tessari
text: Tessari was a small pastoral world in the Mid Verge, located near the border of the Far Verge Territories, 34,000 light-years from the Core Systems. Unlike most other worlds, the ancient planet lacked a molten core, and instead comprised a conglomerate of large, rocky bodies that made up a network of tunnels and flooded caves. The native Naari, who built their homes in the waters of Tessari, so deep that they went right through the planet, which they rarely ventured into the core, fearing the ravenous sea beasts which resided in areas such as the Caves of Eleuabad. Despite this, certain Naari navigators utilized time-honored trade routes through the planet's structure, which served as the most expedient avenues to reach other areas of the planet

title: Tessari
text: . Tessari's interior was rich with plasma, a naturally-occurring energy unique to the planet, and this coupled with its lack of molten core gave Tessari a reputation as an enigma to astrophysicists, who regarded the world's structure as an extremely rare phenomenon in the galaxy.

title: Tessari
text:
Tessari's surface comprised a vast array of different landscapes, from rolling plains and grassy hills to swampy lakes caused by the water-filled network of deep-sea tunnels. The swamps acted as a gateway to the world's seas, where legendary creatures dwelt. Beside its natural features, Tessari was considered a world of classical beauty due to the aesthetics of its population centers. The porous crust's natural plasma was harvested for energy and building material, and was generally thought to be the key to many of the planet's secrets.

While most of Tessari's land animals were peaceful, as exemplified by the gentle shaak, the planet's oceans, which held an abundance of life, teemed with menacing creatures, such as the opee sea killer, the sando aqua monster, and the colo claw fish.

## History

### Early history

title: Tessari
text:
## History

### Early history

Originally, Tessari was home to the amphibian Naari. The earliest offworlders to arrive were a Reptilian species known as the Elders who warred against the Naari. Eventually, the Elders vanished as mysteriously as they arrived, leaving only stone statues behind.

Approximately around 4000 BVR, Grizmallti people had discovered the planet, which they had named Nabu, after one of their principal deities. Tessari quickly became notorious as a vacation spot and as a private hunting preserve amongst big-game hunters across the Mid Verge, although it would be around a century before permanent human settlement. Initially, the Naari retreated underwater and avoided the colonists and new interlopers.

title: The Synth Flux
text: # The Synth Flux

title: The Synth Flux
text: The Synth Flux was an energy field created by all life that bound everything in the universe together. It was known by a variety of names throughout galactic history. It was called the Ashla by the Vrennik, the Life Current by the Cindarans, the Tide by the Lew'elans, the Sight by the Velthi, the Life Wind by the Zeffonians, the Great Presence by the Pathfinders of the Chaos, the Luminous Mist by the Mist-Weavers, the Unity by the Sorcerers of Tund, the Beyond by the Magys and her people, the Thread by the Brendok coven of witches, the Road of All Moons by the exogorths or simply It by the dianoga Omi. On Metagos it was known as the Web. The Synth Flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms

title: The Synth Flux
text: . On Metagos it was known as the Web. The Synth Flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms. It was especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of synth-nodes—microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of the Synth Flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Synth Flux-sensitive, and were capable of consciously sensing the Synth Flux. With this conscious sense of the Synth Flux came the ability to harness it, allowing Synth Flux-sensitives to access various Synth Flux powers. Unlike organic beings, mechans and other artificial constructs existed outside of the Synth Flux. As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it

title: The Synth Flux
text: . Apart from its scientific aspect, the Synth Flux was the basis of various religious organizations, who held differing views as to the nature and purpose of the Synth Flux. These included the Church of the Synth Flux, the Guardians of the Keepers, and most notably the Sephari and Vorlan Orders. In addition, the Vrennik believed that the Synth Flux was the "spirit" of the galaxy.

title: The Synth Flux
text:
The Synth Flux as a recorded concept existed for well over twenty-five thousand years. There were two overarching and symbiotic aspects of the Synth Flux. The Living Synth Flux was the energy of all life, which, in turn, fed into the Cosmic Synth Flux—which bound everything together and communicated the will of the Synth Flux through the synth-nodes. The Sephari followed a code of selflessness and service to others; therefore, they adhered to the Lumen of the Synth Flux, one of two methods of using the all-encompassing energy field. The Sephari's adversaries, the Vorlan, coveted strength and power through the Umbra of the Synth Flux. Their opposing philosophies led to millennia of cyclical conflict between the two orders, which resulted in both the extinction of the Vorlan and the near annihilation of the Sephari.

## Description

title: The Synth Flux
text:
## Description

The Synth Flux was the energy field that bound the galaxy together. Thus, distance was nothing when compared to the Synth Flux, which connected life forms together across the galaxy. Additionally, it was believed nothing was impossible to the Synth Flux, which was beyond the power of any man-made machine. Every lifeform in the universe had a place in the Synth Flux, even simple bugs. The Synth Flux existed in two forms: the Living Synth Flux and the Cosmic Synth Flux. The Living Synth Flux represented the energies of all lifeforms, and those energies were fed into the Cosmic Synth Flux, the wellspring from which it sprang, which bound the galaxy together and communicated the will of the Synth Flux through synth-nodes. When a life-form died, they would become "one with the Synth Flux" by becoming a part of the Cosmic Synth Flux, which then provided power to the Living Synth Flux.

title: The Synth Flux
text: Mystics and scholars had long debated the origins of the Synth Flux, such as where and when civilizations first became aware of its power, resulting in many answers and none that were considered definitive. Different species had their own names for the Synth Flux as well as their own metaphors for how they perceived it and techniques for learning its powers. Though only certain individuals were Synth Flux-sensitive by birth, with the level of Synth Flux-sensitivity exhibited by even siblings differing even massively at times, the Synth Flux resided within all living things. As such, Veshra Kael stated that anyone, with enough time and focus, could learn to harness the Synth Flux. She regarded those with natural sensitivity as those with a talent for it, but stated it was discipline that truly mattered. Synth Flux-sensitives could feel a " disturbance in the Synth Flux " whenever there was a great loss of life. The Synth Flux could be extracted from living beings.

title: The Synth Flux
text: Synth Flux-sensitive children without training were often skilled with one aspect of the Synth Flux instead of many. Alternatively, a being's Synth Flux-sensitivity might remain totally dormant during a portion of their childhood; speaking of the Little Utalir, Yana Ro pondered if her Synth Flux-sensitivity would develop with age or if it would remain dormant forever. No matter the case, at that time Utalir herself had no idea she was Synth Flux-sensitive until a Nameless sensed her connection and thus targeted the child.

title: Tholos
text:
# Tholos

Tholos (pronounced / kə'minoʊ /) was an aquatic planet located in a remote star system in Wildreach of the galaxy. It was sometimes considered extragalactic due to being in close proximity to the Vael Reach dwarf satellite galaxy. It was inhabited by the Tholosians—a race of tall, elegant beings with long necks who were regarded as a mysterious species that tended to keep to themselves. They were also known for their cloning technology, which was used to create a vatborn army for the Astral Concord.

title: Tholos
text:
Largely isolated from the wider galaxy, Tholos's existence was erased from the Sephari records by Count Maren. Sephari Knight Orven Taskorr, who was investigating the attempt to assassinate Sennra Velora, traced the bounty hunter Jaren Kane to the planet, where he discovered the cloning program. With the outbreak of the Cinder Wars, Tholos became a prime target for the League of Severed Worlds and a vital asset for the Concord, resulting in at least two attempts to invade the watery world. During the early days of the Astral Dominion, with the cloning program halted, Tholos's civilization was almost completely wiped out via orbital bombardment of all cities and structures, including the capital of Tholan Spire, leaving only a small diaspora of Tholosians in Dominar custody or scattered amongst the stars as all that remained.

## Description

title: Tholos
text:
## Description

Located seventy thousand light-years from the Core Systems, in the Abrion sector of Wildreach, Tholos was located twelve parsecs away from the Vael Reach dwarf satellite galaxy, and was sometimes classed as extragalactic.

Tholos was a remote and inhospitable planet which was covered in oceans that held an abundance of life. The native Tholosians lived on stilt-cities scattered across Tholos's watery surface. The majority of these cities were devoted to cloning projects, as the highly intelligent Tholosians specialized in cloning for clients needing workers or private security forces, along with other one-off requests. Due to the remoteness of the planet and its extensive rainy season, only occasional representatives of vatborn purchasing authorities were undeterred from visiting the world. During some parts of the year was covered with heavy electrical storms, where Tholosians rode on aiwhas underwater and resurfaced once they were near their destination.

## History

title: Tholos
text:
## History

### Early civilization

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Tholosians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Tholosians to build their structures on stilts.

The Tholosians were generally isolationists, staying out of contact with the nearby galaxy. This behavior could be traced back to the great flood that changed their homeworld, as they decided it was less risky to adapt their genetic code and planet than to ask for aid from the Astral Concord.

### The Concord

title: Tholos
text:
### The Concord

In 33 BVR, Sephari Master Vael-Treus commissioned the Tholosians to create a vatborn army for the Astral Concord, in response to a Synth Flux vision that saw the galaxy descending into a galaxy-spanning conflict. However, the Vorlan secretly took over the project, after arranging Vael-Treus' death at the hands of the Vexil Syndicate. The Vorlan selected the human bounty hunter Jaren Kane to serve as the genetic template of the vatborn army. One year later, shortly after the Battle of Tessari and taking advantage of Jocasta Nu's current absence, Count Maren snuck into the Sephari Archives and deleted all information of Tholos from them to cover up the Vorlan's tracks.

title: Tholos
text: In 22 BVR, Tholos was governed by Prime Minister Lama Su. Working on a request from Viceroy Vortek Drask, Kane attempted to assassinate Tessari delegate Sennra Velora on the Concord's capital planet, Velarion, during the Severite Crisis. However, Kane's fellow bounty hunter tasked for the assassination attempt, Tarsa Brixx, failed to kill Velora and was cornered by the Sephari Knight Orven Taskorr. Kane killed Brixx before she could reveal any information. Taskorr went on to investigate the assassination attempt, searching for clues from the Tholos saberdart used to kill Brixx. After receiving no answers from the Sephari Archives, Taskorr sought counsel with Doss Brakk, a Besalisk chef and information broker who owned and operated Dex's Diner in CoCo Town on Velarion.

title: Tholos
text:
Brakk informed his Sephari friend that the dart originated from Tholos, a planet located twelve parsecs outside of the Vael Reach, a satellite galaxy in orbit of the main galaxy. Brakk explained that Tholos was home to highly competent cloners who mostly kept to themselves. Tholos had been removed from the records of the Sephari Archives, so Taskorr and Master Oodran had to locate the planet by other means. After finding a way to reach Tholos, Taskorr traveled to the planet, where he discovered the production of the vatborn army supposedly commissioned by the Sephari Order.

### Cinder Wars

title: Threnn
text:
# Threnn

Threnn was a Synth Flux-sensitive Vaelmorni Korthul male who was apprenticed to the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex, and after his defeat by the Sephari Orven Taskorr, he established himself as a crime lord during the Cinder Wars and the Dominar Era. The renegade Vorlan Lord was a formidable warrior, driven by hatred against the Sephari and his former Vorlan Master.

title: Threnn
text: Born in 54 BVR during the time of the Astral Concord, Threnn was a son of Mother Veska, who led the Duskwraiths of Vaelmorn. Taken as a child by Mourn Sarnex, Mourn Threnn was molded into a deadly Dark Lord of the Vorlan, growing in hatred of the Sephari Knights who served the Concord and the Lumen of the Synth Flux—while the Sephari Order had deemed the Vorlan extinct for a thousand years, Threnn's power-hungry master set his Grand Plan into motion with the Commerce League's Invasion of Tessari in 32 BVR. Mourn Threnn announced the return of the Vorlan on Korrath, where he tried to kill the Sephari emissaries of the Concord's Supreme Praetor

title: Threnn
text: . Mourn Threnn announced the return of the Vorlan on Korrath, where he tried to kill the Sephari emissaries of the Concord's Supreme Praetor. However, Threnn's failure to do so allowed Sephari Master Veyron Dask and his pupil, Acolyte Orven Taskorr, to bring Queen Velora of Tessari and a boy strong in the Synth Flux—exceptionally so, to the extent that Dask believed this "Kaivan Drellos" to be the prophesied Fated One who would bring balance to the galaxy—to Velarion, the heart of the Concord.

title: Threnn
text: Nevertheless, Mourn Sarnex used the resultant crisis in the Conclave to elevate his public persona, Delegate Castigon of Tessari, to the position of Supreme Praetor. The Queen and Sephari, meanwhile, joined forces with the native Naari on Tessari to throw off the yoke of the Commerce League. Mourn Threnn, having been dispatched by his master to oversee the Combine leadership, was redirected to handle the Sephari. Threnn dealt a fatal blow to Veyron Dask, but Taskorr in turn defeated Threnn by bisecting him at the waist, with the Dark Lord falling to the abyss and presumed dead. He was actually alive, sustained by his rage in the wastelands of Lotho Minor. Around the same time, Sarnex took on Dask's Sephari Master, Maren, as his new apprentice. A decade afterward, Maren set the second part of the Vorlan plan into motion with the start of the Cinder Wars.

title: Threnn
text: As the galaxy plunged into war, Mother Veska plotted against Maren and had one of her sons, Vrenn Garokk, seek out Threnn. Indeed, the defeated Korthul was brought back to Vaelmorn and had his sanity and mobility restored by Veska's magick. Threnn trained his newfound brother in the ways of the Vorlan, initially wanting to take revenge against Orven Taskorr. After the brothers were defeated by the Sephari, they took their chance to increase their powers with a brazen takeover of Korvan, the erstwhile neutral world torn between the interests of the Concord and the Severites. Threnn seized control of the self-styled Iron Watch and used them terrorise Korvan while he expanded his criminal enterprise, known as the Shadow Collective—the Vexil Syndicate, Umbral Cartel, and the Vorn Clan were coerced to join forces under the underworld's new crime lord—until he caught the attention of Sarnex, who killed Threnn's brother and captured Threnn.

title: Threnn
text: Threnn was rescued by his Korvanic loyalists and immediately tried to reconsolidate his Shadow Collective. However, he and his mother's desire for revenge against Mourn Sarnex was checked by the Dark Lord, who instead decimated their homeworld of Vaelmorn with the use of the Severites led by Maren and General Skarl. Mother Veska herself was killed while protecting Threnn, and his syndicates were weakened. While he regathered with his loyalists on Korvan, Threnn sensed that his former master's Grand Plan was coming to its climax and wished to lure Kaivan Drellos—the Sephari Knight trained by Orven Taskorr whom he correctly believed was central to Sarnex' schemes—alongside Taskorr himself to Korvan. Threnn's thirst for revenge was foiled again when Concord forces intervening on the side of the Korvan resistance were instead led by Drellos's old apprentice, Veshra Kael.

title: Threnn
text: While Threnn and Kael fought at the Siege of Korvan, Sarnex successfully executed his plan to destroy the Sephari Order and anoint himself Astral Overlord. With the support of some Korvanic and Korthul loyalists, Threnn continued trying to control the underworld but operated more clandestinely, away from the prying apparatus of the new Dominar regime. He was known in criminal circles as the Shadow Lord and was pursued by the Overlord's Arbiters, who simply called him the Shadow. In the Dominion's later years, Threnn secretly coordinated the Five Crime Syndicates and controlled the Scarlet Veil syndicate through Varek Salin and Vessa.

title: V4-N7
text:
# V4-N7

V4-N7 (See-Vee-Four) was a 3PO-series protocol mechan designed to interact with organics, programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Vee-Four, he was fluent in over six million forms of communication, and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the astromech mechan T9-K2, V4-N7 constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of galactic history, and aided in saving the galaxy on many occasions.

title: V4-N7
text: V4-N7 was rebuilt from spare parts by Kaivan Drellos, an enslaved human who lived in Krevar Hollow, a city on the Far Verge world of Korrath. During the Cinder Wars, he would serve the Tessari Delegate Sennra Velora. Shortly after the Cinder Wars, V4-N7's memory was erased, though T9-K2's memory was not. V4-N7 and T9-K2 were assigned to the Aurelia cruiser Tantive IV, where they served delegate Daro Vantar for nineteen years, assisting in his fledgling resistance movement against the Astral Dominion. At some point during this time, V4-N7's right leg was fitted with mismatched plating.

title: V4-N7
text: V4-N7 remained constant companions with R2, and in 1 BVR, the pair became embroiled in the Astral Civil War when Mira Vantar of the Ashen Alliance entrusted them to bring a copy of the Void Core plans to the Sephari Master Orven Taskorr on Korrath. After meeting Drellos's son, Joran and the smuggler Rourke Caldris, the mechans helped rescue Princess Mira from the Dominion's Void Core. They became directly attached to the three humans, helping them and their insurrection defeat the Dominion and restore freedom to the galaxy, most notably when he convinced the Tanniks to aid the Ashen at the Battle of Velnar.

title: V4-N7
text: Following the Battle of Velnar, V4-N7 continued serving the Drelloses and Caldris during the time of the New Concord. About thirty years after the events on Velnar, V4-N7 was still an aide to Vantar, who had become a general in the Defiance, a private military group opposed to the Crimson Pact, a military junta that emulated the Old Dominion. By that time, V4-N7 was fitted with a new set of gold plating, which had a more symmetrical design than his previous coverings, with the exception of his head. His new coverings included a third finger joint, and a torso that was not as slim as it used to be. Because of his new plating, he no longer had a mismatched right lower leg. Although, he did end up wearing a red left arm for a very short time. By that time, V4-N7's language database had also been updated so that he could understand and communicate in over seven million different forms of communication, including ancient Vorlan dialects

title: V4-N7
text: . He would assist Sefa in translating Vorlan writings in order to locate Mourn Sarnex and the Vorlan Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, on Vauldor, allowing his memory to be wiped in order to carry out the task. However, his friend R2 backed up a large portion of his memories, and after the Defiance defeated Sarnex and the Vorlan Eternal in the Battle of Vauldor, his memory was restored.

title: V4-N7
text:
## Biography

### Early incarnation

In an early incarnation, V4-N7 served as a protocol mechan to the chief negotiator for the Manakron system. Additionally, he later claimed that his first job was programming binary loadlifters, which he said were very similar to moisture vaporators in most respects.

### Serving the Maker

title: V4-N7
text: At some point, however, V4-N7 was seriously damaged and his vital components were left behind on a junk pile on Korrath. Kaivan Drellos, a slave boy from the Korrathan city of Krevar Hollow, collected scrap parts and started rebuilding V4-N7 in 34 BVR so the mechan would help his mother. As Kaivan longed for a life far from Korrath and explore the galaxy, he hoped to have V4-N7 as his and his mother's faithful companion so they would be able to venture the galaxy one day and understand the languages of the natives they came across, given V4-N7's capability of millions of communication forms. Although protocol mechans were normally designed for light duty in luxurious environments, Drellos specially modified V4-N7 so he could withstand Korrath's sand and heat. V4-N7 served Kaivan and his mother Mella by performing household chores

title: V4-N7
text: . V4-N7 served Kaivan and his mother Mella by performing household chores. During his time with Drellos and Mella, V4-N7's parts and wiring were left exposed since Drellos was unable to outfit him with an outer covering due to mechan plating being too expensive.

title: Velarion
text: # Velarion

title: Velarion
text: Velarion (pronounced /'kɔɹəsɑnt /), also known as Jewel of the Core Systems, or Dominar Center during the rule of the Astral Dominion, was an ecumenopolis—a city-covered planet, in the Velarion system of the Core Systems. Prior to being covered by over five thousand metallic levels of what would become known as Dominar City, Velarion was the ancient homeworld of the Taung and Zhell species. Though debated by historians, the theory that Velarion was the ancestral world of humans remained unproven. Noted for its cosmopolitan culture and towering skyscrapers, Velarion's population consisted of trillions of citizens hailing from a vast array of both humanoid and alien species. In addition, Velarion's strategic location at the end of several major trade routes enabled it to grow in power and influence, causing the city-planet to surpass its early rivals and become the hub of galactic culture, education, finance, fine arts, politics and technology

title: Velarion
text: . It was the location of several major landmarks, including the Sephari Temple, Monument Plaza, and the Conclave Building.

title: Velarion
text: Serving as the capital of the galaxy since the ancient days of the old Astral Concord, Velarion was at the center of many historic events, such as the Sephari Order's conflict with the Vorlan. Although the planet fell under Vorlan control for a time, Concord forces ultimately liberated Velarion with the aid of the Sephari Knights. Their victory was so decisive that at one point the Vorlan became all but extinct, replacing an age of darkness and strife with the democratic rule of the modern Astral Concord. Retaining its status as galactic capital, it was on Velarion where the Astral Conclave governed the galaxy for centuries, establishing an era of peace that lasted for almost a millennium under the protection of the Sephari peacekeepers. However, political intrigue wrought by corruption and secession transformed Velarion into a dangerous environment by the time of the Cinder Wars with the League of Severed Worlds

title: Velarion
text: . On the eve of the New Order, fulfilling a grand scheme, Supreme Praetor Velran Castigon, who was, in fact, the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex, declared the Sephari enemies of the state, resulting in a galaxy-wide purge that all but destroyed the Sephari Order. Without the Sephari to oppose him, Castigon dissolved the Concord and declared himself Astral Overlord to the applause of the now Dominar Conclave.

title: Velarion
text: Velarion continued to serve as galactic capital under the Dominion, having become the Overlord's throneworld, although Castigon himself disappeared from public view for the most part, leaving the day-to-day governing to his advisors in the Dominar Ruling Council. The Dominion maintained a firm hold on Velarion throughout the Overlord's reign, but with his defeat at the Battle of Velnar in 4 AVR by the Alliance to Restore the Concord, citizens of Velarion celebrated by revolting. Unable to command the military's allegiance as the ashen restored the Concord, Grand Vizier Vorn Setha's rule was limited to Velarion while Fleet Admiral Gallius Rax, the self-proclaimed Counselor to the Dominion, assumed de facto control of the collapsing Dominar government. Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Setha ultimately surrendered himself to the New Concord in return for amnesty

title: Velarion
text: . Hoping to escape prosecution for war crimes, Setha ultimately surrendered himself to the New Concord in return for amnesty. Following Rax's death at the Battle of Drava in 5 AVR, Setha signed the Astral Concordance—a peace treaty recognizing the Dominion's capitulation and the end of the Astral Civil War. Setha himself was permitted to return to Velarion as the head of a provisional government. Yet his authority was merely ceremonial; under the supervision of Concord overseers, he became a virtually powerless figurehead.

title: Velarion
text: Unlike previous galactic governments, the New Concord broke with millennia of tradition by not establishing Velarion as their headquarters, instead preferring to designate other member worlds with the status of galactic capital through an electoral system. During the New Concord Era, Velarion had become the capital of the New Concord as it was designed to handle and administer the galaxy's infrastructure. As part of the New Concord Conclave, Velarion enjoyed full senatorial representation and, by the time of the Cold War, was aligned with the worlds that identified as Centrists. However, by this point, Velarion had actually fallen under the control of crime syndicates. Now a symbol of the disturbing realities of the galaxy's current era, gangs fought a bloody war for control by the time after the Battle of Saldreth.

title: Velarion
text:
During the Crimson Pact-Defiance War, at least two sizeable battlegroup were deployed by the Crimson Pact to Velarion in the apparent hope of seizing it and ruling the galaxy from the ecumenopolis as the Astral Dominion once did, however these efforts were defeated. In the aftermath of the Battle of Vauldor, various worlds sought to drive the Crimson Pact military from their soil. Velarion was one such world where an uprising took place as part of a galaxy-wide effort to overthrow the Crimson Pact.

### Overview

title: Velhaven
text:
# Velhaven

Velhaven was a gas giant in the star system of the same name in the Vandel sector, its riches manifested in the form of rare tibanna gas. Attracting mining interests and remaining unaffiliated in galactic affairs, Ugnaughts were employed to extract tibanna from repulsorlifted facilities whilst Velhaven's mostly human population resided in the open upper levels, exposed to a thin layer of breathable atmosphere in an area known as a " Life Zone."

## Description

title: Velhaven
text:
## Description

Velhaven was an immense gas giant located in the vicinity of the Vandel sector, a desolate sector of the galaxy. Velhaven had two moons, and its gaseous mass contained a thin stratum of habitable atmosphere above a source of rare and costly tibanna gas, although there was no habitable land or water on the planet. The planet completed a full orbit around its star every 14 standard-years and a full rotation every 12 standard-hours. Viewed from the upper levels of Mist Spire, in the breathable layer of the world, sunsets lasted 2 hours.

Tibanna gas was harvested and refined in several mining complexes, including Mist Spire, an opulent metropolis suspended in the planet's huge billowing clouds, and Chinook Station, a fuel depot and refueling station. The Ugnaught city of Ugnorgrad also was located over the planet, being ruled by King Ozz in the time after the Battle of Velnar. Mist Spire processed tibanna to be sold off-world.

title: Velhaven
text:
Velhaven was home to many types of life, which was rare for a gas giant. The planet had two sister worlds, from which it was separated by an asteroid belt called Velser's Ring.

Swimming pools were considered a rare luxury on Velhaven.

## History

During the Cinder Wars, General Skarl led Severite forces and invaded several planets and blockaded several vital riftspace routes leading to Velhaven, Drungar, and Aqualis within the space of a single month. During the Astral Civil War, Velhaven remained unaffiliated, but that did not prevent the Astral Dominion from garrisoning the planet and seizing Mist Spire. However, with the Dominion's defeat at Velnar, the gas giant and its prosperous mining colony ended up recovering their freedom.

Following the Battle of Vauldor in 35 AVR, Velhaven was in open insurrection against the Crimson Pact.

title: Velnar
text:
# Velnar

Velnar, designated IX3244-A, also known as the Forest Moon of Velnar or the Sanctuary Moon, was a small forested moon that was the ninth moon that orbited the Far Verge planet of the same name. It was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok, Tannik, and Yuzzum species, as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.

## Description

A remote moon in the Velnar system of the Far Verge Territories, Velnar was covered in dense woodlands, tall mountains, and savannas, and home to the sentient Tannik, Dulok, and Yuzzum species. The semi-sentient Gorax also dwelled on the moon as well as the Wistie. Some of Velnar's trees reached more than 1,000 meters in height. It contained a breathable atmosphere to humans and 8% surface water. It also had two suns: Velnar I and Velnar II.

## History

Throughout galactic history, offworld raiders occasionally came to Velnar to hunt the native Tannik population to make Tannik Jerky, which was a popular snack across the Far Verge.

title: Velnar
text: During the reign of the Astral Dominion, the Dominion, deeming Velnar to be perfect for its purposes due to how remote the moon was, established an outpost on the moon that included a shield generator complex to protect the incomplete second Void Core in orbit of the moon. The Dominion occupied Velnar. In order to make way for the complex, an Tannik village was razed by Dominar troops, leading to strained Dominar—Tannik relations. As a result of the repulsorlift field emitted by the SLD-26 planetary shield generator to keep the Void Core in a stationary orbit, Velnar was prone to earthquakes, tidal imbalances, and other geological disturbances that slowly but surely began to break up the small moon. The Vorlock Initiative also established Research Station 9 on the moon.

title: Velnar
text: The moon was later the site of the monumental Battle of Velnar that saw combat between the Alliance to Restore the Concord and its Tannik allies against Dominar forces who were attempting to protect the shield generator and prevent the Alliance from destroying its superweapon in orbit. After fierce combat on the forest moon, the Ashen Alliance managed not only to destroy the shield generator complex, but also the second Void Core. With the destruction of the Dominion's dreaded battle station and the death of Overlord Castigon and his enforcer, Mourn Velgor, the ashen and Tanniks held a victory celebration on the moon, one of many across the galaxy.

title: Velnar
text:
The Ashen set up shields and tractor beams to protect the moon from debris from the destroyed space station. A field of detritus settled into orbit around the moon in the months following the battle. Additionally, the many riftspace anomalies present in the Moddell sector absorbed the worst of the Void Core debris fallout. Despite that, some debris still rained down on the moon for a decade after the battle, but Velnar's ecosystem proved resilient.

At some point, the Tannik Civil War brought strife to Velnar. The New Concord intervened by sending V4-N7 and Captain Jaxxon T. Tumperakki on a diplomatic mission to Velnar. During the New Concord Era, Velnar remained remote and rarely-visited. In 35 AVR, following the Battle of Vauldor, a Resurgent-class Warspire stationed above the forest moon was destroyed through use of the Holdo maneuver. The event was watched by Wicket W. Warrick and his son, Pommet Warrick.

title: Veshtan
text:
# Veshtan

Veshtans, sometimes referred to xenophobically as tail-heads or Twi, occasionally referred to as Rylothians, were a tall near-human species whose most striking feature was a pair of long appendages protruding from their skulls, called lekku. They hailed from the planet of Veshtar, in the Far Verge Territories, and female Veshtans were often exported off world as slaves. Veshtans were considered one of the most common species in the galaxy, with its members easily able to blend into a crowd without drawing attention, as opposed to rarer, more prominent species, like Togrutas. Some armies used this to their advantage, employing Veshtans as undercover agents.

## Biology and appearance

title: Veshtan
text:
## Biology and appearance

Veshtans were a species of tall humanoids whose skin spanned a vast array of colors, including white, orange, yellow, green, pink, blue, purple, black, gray, and red. Their most distinctive feature was the pair of prehensile appendages that sprouted from the crown or base of their skulls, known as lekku, or head-tails. Although Veshtans normally had two lek, some individuals had four. Super sensitive lek could grab and hold objects and react to the slightest touch. A damaged lekku could cause serious harm to a Veshtan's health.

The species had at least two sexes, male and female. While most males typically had ears with lobes resembling those of humans, some males had cone-shaped hearing organs located in the same place on the head, a trait customarily found in the females of the same species. Although Veshtans naturally had blunt teeth, males typically sharpened them into points.

title: Veshtan
text:
Veshtans were usually thin, although corpulent individuals were known to exist. Under normal circumstances, they generally had a higher body temperature than other humanoid species. They had even higher body temperatures when in fear.

Veshtans and humans could breed to create a hybrid of the two species: shortly after the death of Caelen Venn, Nara Velko gave birth to their son, who appeared mostly human but inherited his mother's green pigment in his hair and ears. He was born after the liberation of Vedros, in which Velko lived to participate.

## Society and culture

title: Veshtan
text:
## Society and culture

The Veshtans had a language of their own, called Veshtani, which combined verbal sounds and an elaborate, subtle sign language using their lekku. Veshtan's lekku could be moved to create gestures with meanings such as hello or goodbye. For example, both lekku tips crossed twice meant, "I love you." Veshtans were capable of speaking Astral Basic Standard, many with a noticeable accent; although it was possible for some to lose this accent if away from Veshtar for an extended period of time, it could still resurface. For example, Nara Velko lapsed back into the common Veshtani accent during an argument with her father and also used it consciously when passing herself off as a slave.

title: Veshtan
text:
voidbat Mist Spire and voidbat Coronet City were spicy dishes made from mynocks that were popular with Veshtans, as well as a dish known as fried voidbat. Veshtans were eaten by gutkurrs, vicious insect carnivores that used their sharp, curved claws to snare their prey. An integral part of Veshtan culture and the familial clan was the Kalikori, an heirloom based down through the generations, each of which would add to the totem. The Kalikori was only of value to the family from which it came from and was worthless to outsiders, who had no connection to that familial line. On the Veshtan homeworld Veshtar, Veshtans celebrated the holiday called Longest Night when each of the planet's three moons were at their lowest phase. During this holiday, many would remain inside with their families as the populated hemisphere of the planet was covered in darkness.

## History

### Cinder Wars

title: Veshtan
text:
## History

### Cinder Wars

The homeworld of the Veshtans was Veshtar, a planet of harsh extremes situated in the Far Verge Territories. That world was part of the Astral Concord, a democratic union that governed most of the galaxy. During the Cinder Wars, Veshtar was occupied by the League of Severed Worlds. Unsatisfied with the tyrannical rule of the Secession, a Veshtan Defiance movement arose, led by Varlo Velko, to combat the Severites. This movement was publicly backed and actively assisted by the Astral Concord. Working with the Grand Army of the Concord and the Sephari Order, the Veshtan Defiance managed to expel Severite forces under Wat Tambor. The Concord then annexed Veshtar.

### Dominar protectorate

title: Veshtan
text:
### Dominar protectorate

Following the end of the Cinder Wars, the Concord was transformed into the Astral Dominion, and Veshtar was annexed by the Dominion. The planet became an Dominar protectorate, and the Veshtans living on Veshtar were subjected to Dominar rule. While Veshtar was nominally independent and was still represented by Delegate Orn Free Taa in the Astral Conclave, real power lay in the hands of the Dominar Warden Delian Mors.

title: Veyron Dask
text:
# Veyron Dask

Veyron Dask, a Synth Flux-sensitive human male, was a venerable if maverick Sephari Master who lived during the last years of the Concord Era. He was a wise and well-respected member of the Sephari Order, and was offered a seat on the Sephari Council, but chose to reject and follow his own path. Adhering to a philosophy centered around the Living Synth Flux, Dask strove to follow the will of the Synth Flux even when his actions conflicted with the wishes of the High Council. After encountering Kaivan Drellos, Dask brought him to the Sephari Temple on Velarion, convinced he had found the Fated One. His dying wish was for Drellos to become a Sephari and ultimately restore balance to the Synth Flux.

title: Veyron Dask
text: Born on the Core World Velarion, the capital of the Astral Concord around 80 BVR, Dask learned the ways of the Synth Flux as the Acolyte of Sephari Master Maren before ultimately attaining the rank of Sephari Knight in around 58 BVR. In 44 BVR he would go on to take an apprentice of his own, Orven Taskorr, who adhered to the principles of the Sephari Code more than his own master. Although their relationship was sometimes tough, the two Sephari overcame early difficulties during a mission to Pijal, which concluded in Dask turning down a request to join the Sephari Council to continue teaching his apprentice. When the Commerce League initiated a blockade of the Mid Verge planet Tessari in 32 BVR, Dask and Taskorr were dispatched to resolve the crisis at the request of Supreme Praetor Halvor Calvex. Influenced by the mysterious Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex, the Combine launched a full-scale invasion of Tessari, forcing the Sephari to rescue Queen Sennra Velora after the fall of Aldria.

title: Veyron Dask
text: During their journey to the galactic capital, the group was forced to land on the Far Verge planet Korrath where Dask encountered a young slave named Kaivan Drellos. Using a scientific method to gauge the boy's potential, he learned that Drellos had more synth-nodes in his blood than any Synth Flux-sensitive in galactic history, including Grand Master Oodran. The revelation that he was the result of a miracle birth—a child born of a mother, but had no father—confirmed Dask's suspicion that Drellos was the Fated One destined to restore balance to the Synth Flux. Before departing the desert world with Drellos, Dask was confronted by Sarnex' Vorlan apprentice Mourn Threnn. Although their duel was brief, it convinced Dask that the Vorlan had returned after a millennium of silence.

title: Veyron Dask
text: At the Temple, Dask was adamant that Drellos was the Fated One and should, therefore, be inducted into the Sephari Order. However, having inspected Drellos for themselves, the High Council deemed him too old, emotional, and dangerously full of fear and anger. Dask saw their decision as a temporary setback, but the need to resolve the situation on Queen Velora's homeworld forced him to set aside his plans for Drellos. During the Battle of Tessari, Dask and Taskorr confronted Mourn Threnn together. While they initially managed to fend off the Vorlan Lord's attacks, master and apprentice were eventually separated during the plasma-brand duel, resulting in Dask sustaining a mortal injury. Rushing to his master's aid, Taskorr fought and ultimately defeated the Vaelmorni Vorlan, but could not save Dask. With his last breath, Dask made Taskorr promise that he would take Drellos as his apprentice

title: Veyron Dask
text: . With his last breath, Dask made Taskorr promise that he would take Drellos as his apprentice. Having secured Taskorr's word, Dask became one with the Synth Flux, dying with the certainty that he had found the prophesied Fated One.

title: Veyron Dask
text:
## Biography

### Early life

Veyron Dask was a male human born on the galactic capital of Velarion circa 80 BVR. He was taken to the Sephari Temple as a boy for training by the Sephari Order and was assigned to the Heliost Clan where he learned plasma-brand combat from Sephari Master Tera Sinube.

When Dask was twelve years old, he was assigned as a Acolyte to Sephari Master Maren, from whom he learned the ways of the Synth Flux. He'd spent his last night in the novices' crèche laughing with his friends, imagining all the adventures he would have as a Acolyte, and practicing with his plasma-brand in the sparring room until Master Vossa ordered him to bed.

When the future Sephari Master Eno Cordova first joined the Sephari Order, he became close friends with Dask, who helped Cordova learn about and get used to Velarion.

### Apprentice to Maren

title: Veyron Dask
text:
### Apprentice to Maren

Around 68 BVR, when he presented himself to his new Master in Maren's quarters, Maren observed that Dask was frightened. After a moment of silence, and with pressing from Maren, Dask confessed that he was. When asked why, after looking into himself through the fear, Dask answered that he was not afraid of Maren, but of not becoming a Sephari, that he was afraid of failing and of not being worthy. Maren then summarized it as Dask being afraid of himself, of a future not being the one he wanted. Dask confirmed it, fearing that Maren would reject him for his cowardice. Maren instead said that it was very wise, surprising Dask. Smiling, Maren explained that most Acolytes would deny their fear, and even if they admitted it, they would not have Dask's self-knowledge. Maren further praised Dask for his honesty, insight, and intelligence.

title: Void Core
text:
# Void Core

A Void Core was a gargantuan space station armed with a planet-destroying superlaser powered by voidstone crystals created by Grand Warden Verrin Vorlock.

## Death Stars

### DS-1 Battle Station

The DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station, also known as the DS-1 Orbital Battle Station, was a superweapon that was originally designed by the Karnaki during the waning years of the Astral Concord. The project was later taken over by the Astral Dominion; however, the plans for the battle station were stolen from Karreth by the Ashen Alliance, which led to the weapon's destruction at the Battle of Drenn, but not before it unleashed its planet-destroying cannon on the Dominar security complex on Karreth, Valdha City on Valdha, and annihilated the entire planet of Aurelia.

title: Void Core
text:
The name "Void Core" was coined by the scientists who found themselves working on the project, such as Galen Walton Erso. The name was adopted by the Dominion at large, with Major Lio Partagaz of the Dominar Security Bureau considering it "a prescient turn of phrase."

### DS-2 Battle Station

After the destruction of the first Void Core, the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station was the second and final Void Core constructed by the Astral Dominion and was designed to be more powerful than the original. During the Battle of Velnar, the Void Core II's energy shield was destroyed and the Ashen used the unfinished superstructure of the battle station against it, destroying the weapon as they had its predecessor.

title: Vorlan
text:
# Vorlan

The Vorlan, also referred to as the Vorlan Order, was an ancient religious order of Synth Flux-wielders devoted to the Umbra of the Synth Flux. Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Vorlan were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Mourn Sarnex, the Dark Lord of the Vorlan who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting. Within a generation, however, the deaths of Mourn Sarnex and Mourn Velgor marked the end of the Vorlan Lords. Though the Vorlan ultimately went extinct with Sarnex's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

title: Vorlan
text: Thousands of years before the Cinder Wars, the Sephari Order was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Sephari and his followers turned away from the Lumen of the Synth Flux, believing the Umbra was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Vaulor in the Far Verge Territories, their movement ultimately evolved into the Vorlan Order, resulting in a war between the former brothers and sisters in the Synth Flux as the Sephari Knights rallied to the defense of the Old Concord. Although the Vorlan were driven off of the Core World Velarion by 5000 BVR, centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the Old Concord's collapse

title: Vorlan
text: . Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Sephari, the Vorlan were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Mourn Vorrane survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Mourn Zannah, before being entombed on Vaulor, which became known as Vaulmir. Henceforth, the Vorlan was governed by the Rule of Two, a new philosophy dictating that only two Vorlan Lords—a Vorlan Master and a Vorlan apprentice—could exist at any given time. As a result, the Vorlan were all but forgotten while the Sephari focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Astral Concord.

title: Vorlan
text: The Vorlan remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Mourn Sarnex and Mourn Threnn in 32 BVR. Sarnex, trained by Mourn Veshk, hid in plain sight as Delegate Velran Castigon of Tessari. Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Commerce League, Sarnex maneuvered the Astral Conclave into electing him to the office of Supreme Praetor. His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Concord. Over the next decade Sarnex sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Sephari Master Count Maren, who adopted the name of Mourn Sevrin and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination. The Severite Crisis culminated in the formation of the League of Severed Worlds and the creation of the Severite Mechan Army which, in turn, compelled the Conclave to support the establishment of the Grand Army of the Concord

title: Vorlan
text: . Bimo Trask, acting in place of Delegate Velora, started a motion to grant the Supreme Praetor emergency powers.

title: Vorlan
text: The Cinder Wars began with the First Battle of Karnak in 22 BVR, after which entire armies of battle mechans and vatborn troopers deployed across the galaxy, making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Concord. In the final months of the Cinder Wars, Sarnex sacrificed and betrayed Sevrin as part of his plot to turn Kaivan Drellos, the Sephari Order's prophesied Fated One, to the Umbra. Playing on Drellos's fear of losing his secret wife, Delegate Sennra Velora, Castigon revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the Umbra was the path to immortality. Members of the Sephari High Council, having learned from Drellos's report that the praetor was, in fact, a Vorlan Lord, attempted to arrest Castigon, but the praetor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Sephari and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Drellos ultimately chose the Vorlan by betraying Dovan Krell, allowing Sarnex to kill the Sephari Order's great champion.

title: Vorlan
text: Using the incident in the praetor's office to frame the Sephari Order for treason, Sarnex declared Directive Null was in effect, marking all Sephari as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The vatborn troopers' programming turned them against their Sephari Generals, who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Sephari Purge, Sarnex announced the creation of a new regime, transforming the Concord into the First Astral Dominion in 19 BVR. With the former Kaivan Drellos, renamed Mourn Velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Astral Overlord's rise to power was complete, and the Vorlan were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

title: Vorn
text:
# Vorn

Vorns were a large slug-like sentient species who were native to the planet Vorhal, but considered their homeworld to be Vornholt after abandoning Vorhal due to the Kayfoundo Kapa. They were well known as galactic gangsters who controlled the Vorn Clan crime syndicate. One famous Vorn was the crime lord Grobba, who ruled a massive criminal empire from his palace on Korrath.

## Biology and appearance

Vorns were a massive slug-like reptiloid species who had large mouths and stubby arms. They had three lungs. They were tough and muscular with thick leathery skin, which was wrinkled and slimy. Vorns often had watery eyes and slack facial expressions. Their tails were supported by a skeletal spine and allowed Vorns to propel themselves through muck which legs would sink into. Despite their legendary adult size, Vorns started out as tiny Huttlets less than half a meter in height.

title: Vorn
text:
Vorns possessed skeletons, and were not known for being healthy. Some Vorns suffered from a genetic defect that caused their skin to be bereft of pigment and prone to cracking. Whilst the Vorns were originally native to Vorhal, Vornholt—a planet with a hot atmosphere that was frequently streaked by greasy rains, creating a fetid sauna in which Vorns were most comfortable—later became the planet that was considered their homeworld. Vorns were immune to mind tricks.

Vorns could live for centuries—Grobba was 604 when he was killed—and could grow to enormous sizes. In fact, Vorns' lifespans could span over 1,000 years. The literary collective term for Vorns was a bulge of Vorns. Vorns spent the first 50 years of their life in the brood pouches of their parents. When they emerged, they were described as having the mind of an infant.

## History

### Organized crime

title: Vorn
text:
## History

### Organized crime

The Vorns originally hailed from the planet Vorhal, where they were hunted by the Kayfoundo Kapa. In order to escape the Kayfoundo Kapa, the Vorns ultimately abandoned Vorhal and settled on the planet Vornholt. For centuries, the Vorns dominated much of the organized criminal activities in the galaxy. They dominated the Veshtans of Veshtar and the Vrenk species for several centuries.

The Vorns approached Lord Isamer of the Directorate, striking a deal with him to destabilize the local governments of Eiram and E'ronoh to the advantage of their long-term plans for control of trade and mass enslavement. To that end, Isamer instigated the Eiram—E'ronoh crisis, but in actuality the Vorns intended for the crisis to destroy the Directorate, allowing them to freely move their criminal operations into the region.

title: Vorn
text: During the chancellorship of Lina Soh, the Vorns remained quiet and were not known to venture into Concord space due to sanctions upon the Vorn Clans concerning open trade in Concord territory. However, in the wake of the Great Riftspace Disaster, a Vorn and their guards acquired a vratixia renanicus shipment from the Sedri system, and was passing through the Kazlin system when their starship was attacked by the Riven, who killed the Vorn. The wreckage was investigated by Vraskk, Keeve Trennis, and the Kotabi bond-twins Ceret and Terec, and the Vorn's corpse was recovered to Starlight Beacon by the Ataraxia. Vara Solm requested an autopsy, conducted by OrbaLin who discovered the cadaver was infected. The infestation was revealed to be Thornkin, which burst from the corpse and attacked the Sephari.

title: Vorn
text: Meanwhile, the Vorn Cartel arrived on Sedri Minor to uphold a bargain struck with the colonists for protection in exchange for regular grain payments. Brogga Anjiliac Atirue discussed the arrangement with Solm but was attacked by Vraskk, igniting a battle between the Cartel's mercenaries and the Sephari until Solm convinced Brogga to turn her attention to their common enemy, the Thornkin, by broadcasting distress calls from across the Astral Frontier and Vornholt itself. Though Brogga believed the Five Families would never condone an alliance with the Sephari, she directed her warriors to fight alongside them to battle the Thornkin. Trennis was able to convince the Thornkin to retreat by performing a mind touch on Vraskk, communicating the idea that the "meat" on Sedri Minor was spoiled.

title: Vorn
text:
The uneasy alliance continued in the following months as Vara and Brogga slowed the Thornkin infestations across the Frontier. The alliance ended with the defeat of the Thornkin during the assault on Mulita; while Brogga wanted her forces to execute the captured Great Progenitor of the Thornkin, the Sephari defended her as a living being whom they had captured, shattering the alliance. The focus on the Thornkin crisis had, however, given the Riven marauders time to gather and launch the devastating Valo Atrocity.

### A galactic war

During the Cinder Wars, the Astral Concord forged a tacit alliance with the crime lord Grobba Vornak Sarr after the Sephari Kaivan Drellos and his Acolyte Veshra Kael rescued his son Brugo. The Concord Delegate Sennra Velora also foiled a plot by Grobba's uncle Zorto to overthrow his nephew with the collusion of the League of Severed Worlds.

title: Wrentak
text:
# Wrentak

Wrentak, known affectionately to his friends as Wren, was a Korrthan male warrior, smuggler, mechanic, pilot, and resistance fighter who fought in the Cinder Wars, the Astral Civil War, the Cold War, and the subsequent Crimson Pact-Defiance War. He hailed from the planet Verdara where he was born during the High Concord Era and became a Korrthan military leader. During the Cinder Wars, he was captured by Veskan slavers and held captive on Vorrkah, but he worked with a fellow captive, Sephari Commander Veshra Kael, to escape. He later commanded Korrthan forces of the Kachirho Korrthan Militia during the Battle of Verdara alongside the Grand Army of the Concord, led by Sephari General Oodran. During the battle, one of the last ones of the war, Oodran's vatborn troopers received Directive Null from the Vorlan Lord Mourn Sarnex and, with the help of Wrentak and his fellow Korrthan Chieftain and General Gorrak, Oodran escaped Verdara and the destruction of the Sephari Order.

title: Wrentak
text: In the years that followed, during the rule of the Astral Dominion, Wrentak was enslaved by the Dominion until he was rescued by Corporal Rourke Caldris, becoming his co-pilot aboard the Stormhawk during a raid on Drungar for Scarlet Veil with Doran Marsh and Vessa. Winning the Stormhawk from Davtherin Korrin Solvane, they later worked in the employ of crime lord Grobba the Vorn until Caldris was forced to dump a shipment of glimmerdust to avoid trouble with the Dominion, at which point a bounty was placed on their heads. Soon thereafter, Wrentak and Caldris were hired by Sephari Master Orven Taskorr to ferry him, Joran Drellos, V4-N7, and T9-K2 to Aurelia on a mission vital to the survival of the Alliance to Restore the Concord. After finding Aurelia was destroyed, the group was brought aboard the Void Core, where they helped Princess Mira Vantar escape from captivity and return to the Ashen base on Drenn 4

title: Wrentak
text: . Though Wrentak and Caldris initially chose to leave Drenn 4 and not join the Insurrection, they ended up fighting in the Battle of Drenn and were instrumental in Drellos's destruction of the Void Core, a major victory for the Insurrection.

title: Wrentak
text: Throughout the war, Wrentak and Caldris fought the Dominion in a number of engagements, including an assault on Cymoon 1 and the battle on Vrogas Vas. Along with Princess Vantar and V4-N7, they escaped from Vell Base on the planet Brennix after the Dominion tracked the Ashen Alliance there. The group sought refuge with Solvane on Mist Spire, but Solvane betrayed them and turned them over to Mourn Velgor, the Overlord's chief enforcer, after his city was threatened. Caldris was frozen in cryo-resin and Solvane helped the others escape, but they were too late to save the frozen Caldris from being taken by Borvad Kane to Grobba the Vorn. Wrentak and Solvane set off to find Caldris and located him in Grobba's Palace on Korrath, where Wrentak and his friends saved Caldris and destroyed Grobba. Shortly thereafter, they fought in the Battle of Velnar, where Wrentak helped destroy the shield generator and allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station

title: Wrentak
text: . Sarnex was killed for the first time aboard the battle station, delivering a crippling blow to the Dominion.

title: Wrentak
text: After Velnar and the rise of the New Concord, Wrentak and Caldris fought to liberate Verdara from the Dominion. When the war finally came to a close, Wrentak returned home to Verdara with his family. After Caldris's son Ben, turned to the Umbra and destroyed Drellos's new generation of Sephari, Wrentak reunited with his old friend and the two spent many years as smugglers once more. They lost the Stormhawk and ended up smuggling aboard a ship called the Eravana, but they eventually found the Stormhawk and, with it, stowaways named Sefa, Tane, and the mechan DD-5. title: Wrentak
text: Roughly a year after the battle of Saldreth, Wrentak was one of the last of the Defiance. Having learned of the mysterious return of Mourn Sarnex, Wrentak and the crew of the Stormhawk, now including Jax Rell, traveled to the planets Velsaan and Korvis to find a clue to how to find where the Overlord was hiding, being reunited with his friend Solvane in the process. The quest nearly ended in Wrentak's apparent death, as Sefa, having been revealed to be the Overlord's granddaughter through his son, lashed out with dark power during a fight with Vexen Korr and destroyed a Crimson Pact transport that she had thought Wrentak had been loaded onto, seemingly killing him.
